column88: According to a transcript of the Deputy Chief Medical Officer's press conference which was published on 7 March 2020, COVID-19 testing was recommended for travellers returning from countries considered to have a high or medium COVID-19 risk. However, testing was considered to be a clinical decision to be negotiated with an individual's doctor. Some States and Territories specifically advised individuals to speak with their doctors to discuss testing.  Other Australian Government media releases (such as one published on 3 March 2020) only mentioned COVID-19 testing for individuals who had returned from overseas or come into close contact with COVID-19 cases who had returned from overseas.  The limited testing availability in place was a continuation of existing measures.  Archived links: https://web.archive.org/web/20220329040340/https://www.health.gov.au/news/deputy-chief-medical-officers-press-conference-about-covid-19 https://web.archive.org/web/20210410144634/https://www.health.gov.au/news/chief-medical-officer-and-minister-hunts-joint-press-conference-on-coronavirus-covid-19

column74: According to a joint media released published by the Australian Minister for Health and the Chief Medical Officer published on 2 March 2020, healthcare and residential aged care workers arriving in Australia from Italy and South Korea were asked not to attend work for 14 days after arriving in Australia. This was an escalation of public health advice directed towards individuals arriving from Italy and South Korea.    Existing travel restrictions imposed on individuals arriving from China and Iran remained the same:  Foreign nationals who had been in Iran or China within the past 14 days were prohibited from entering Australia. Australian citizens, permanent residents and immediate family members who had been in Iran or China in the past 14 days were required to quarantine at home for 14 days after arriving in Australia.     Archived links:  https://web.archive.org/web/20220121004113/https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22media%2Fpressrel%2F7216775%22  https://web.archive.org/web/20220121011945/https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22media%2Fpressrel%2F7218407%22

According to a joint media release from the Australian Prime Minister, the Minister for Health, and the Minister for Foreign Affairs and Minister for Women, foreign nationals who had been in the Republic of Korea on or after 5 March 2020 were prohibited from entering Australia for 14 days from the time they had left or transited through Korea. Australian citizens, permanent residents and immediate family members who had been in Iran in the past 14 days were required to quarantine at home for 14 days after arriving in Australia.   Enhanced health screening and temperature checking arrangements were implemented for individuals arriving in Australia from Italy during this time.    This was a tightening of measures imposed on individuals arriving from the Republic of Korea and Italy. Existing travel restrictions imposed on individuals arriving from China and Iran remained the same:  Foreign nationals who had been in Iran or China within the past 14 days were prohibited from entering Australia. Australian citizens, permanent residents and immediate family members who had been in Iran or China in the past 14 days were required to quarantine at home for 14 days after arriving in Australia.     Archived links:  https://web.archive.org/web/20220121001025/https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22media%2Fpressrel%2F7223641%22  https://web.archive.org/web/20220121011945/https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22media%2Fpressrel%2F7218407%22

As published on the Department of Home Affairs website, The Australian Government announced on 12 March 2020 that travel restrictions will continue to apply to travellers arriving from any part of mainland China, Iran, Republic of Korea and Italy.    Foreign nationals (excluding permanent residents of Australia) who have been in the following countries will not be allowed to enter Australia for 14 days from the time they have left or transited through:  mainland China  Iran  Republic of Korea  Italy.  Australian citizens and permanent residents will still be able to enter, as will their immediate family members (spouses, legal guardians or dependants only). They will be required to self-isolate at home for 14 days from the day they left China, Iran, the Republic of Korea or Italy.  Australia will deny entry to anyone who has left or transited a country subject to travel restrictions within the previous 14 days, with the exception of:  Australian citizens  permanent residents  New Zealand citizens resident in Australia  immediate family members of Australian citizens and permanent residents including spouses, minor dependants and legal guardians diplomats.  This represents a continuation of the policy response.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200314024611/https://www.homeaffairs.gov.au/news-media/current-alerts/novel-coronavirus

column74: According to the Home Affair, from the 15th of March 2020, the Australia Government announced:  - All travellers to Australia will be required to self-isolate for 14 days   - A ban on cruise liners from foreign ports arriving at Australian ports for 30 days    Noting that foreign nationals (excluding permanent residents of Australia) who have been in the following countries will not be allowed to enter Australia for 14 days from the time they have left or transited through:  - Mainland China  - Iran  - Republic of Korea  - Italy    Main source:  https://web.archive.org/web/20200318062142/https://www.homeaffairs.gov.au/news-media/current-alerts/novel-coronavirus
column88: On 20th of March 2020, according to the Australia's Department of Health, it was mentioned that doctor will tell you if you should be tested. The criteria being:  - You have returned from overseas in the past 14 days and you develop respiratory illness with or without fever  - You have been in close contact with a confirmed COVID-19 case in the past 14 days and you develop respiratory illness with or without fever  - You have severe community-acquired pneumonia and there is no clear cause  - You are a healthcare worker who works directly with patients and you have a respiratory illness and a fever    The rational for this is because there is a global shortage of the test kits that pathologists use to diagnose COVID-19. This is why we are doing targeted testing instead of widespread testing.    Main source:  https://web.archive.org/web/20200321051456/https://www.health.gov.au/news/health-alerts/novel-coronavirus-2019-ncov-health-alert/what-you-need-to-know-about-coronavirus-covid-19

column51: From March 17, 2020, public transport in Canberra continued to operate, but with increased COVID-19 measures such as additional cleaning, no longer accepting cash payment of fares, and social distancing. column115: As of 17th of March, according to the Australia's Department of Health, the Residential Aged Care Facilities are operating differently when compared to non-Covid period. This includes: limiting visits to a short duration, maximum of two visitors at one time per day, & no large group visits.    Visitors can't visit if:  - Those who have returned from overseas in the last 14 days.  - Those who have been in contact with a confirmed case of COVID-19 in the last 14 days.  - Those with fever or symptoms of acute respiratory infection (e.g. cough, sore throat, runny nose, shortness of breath) symptoms.  - Those who have not been vaccinated against influenza (after 1st May 2020).    Main source:  https://web.archive.org/web/20200321051253/https://www.health.gov.au/news/australian-health-protection-principal-committee-ahppc-coronavirus-covid-19-statement-on-17-march-2020    Additional source:  https://web.archive.org/web/20200414110933/https://www.health.gov.au/news/advice-for-aged-care-facilities-and-visitors-to-residents

column88: Testing is available for more people who meet the newly expanded testing criteria:    - Travellers from overseas with onset of respiratory symptoms within 14 days of return.  - Close contacts of confirmed COVID-19 cases with respiratory symptoms or fever within 14 days of last contact.  - Healthcare workers with recent onset of respiratory symptoms AND fever irrespective of travel history.   - Patients admitted to hospital with acute respiratory illness or unexplained fever  - Patients with acute respiratory illness or unexplained fever in other high risk settings, such aged care facilities, residential care facilities, boarding schools, and cruise ships.  - Patients with acute respiratory illness or fever presenting with reported links to settings where COVID-19 outbreaks have occurred, in discussion with CDC.    https://web.archive.org/web/20200330072544/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/news-articles/covid-19-testing-criteria-expanded

column15: The ACT Minister for Education and Early Childhood announced that from Tuesday 24 March 2020 all ACT Public Schools will go pupil free until the school holidays. This represents a tightening of restrictions on school attendance as the first such restrictions in place.     https://web.archive.org/web/20211229080617/https://www.education.act.gov.au/about-us/all-news-and-news-alerts/news-items/march-2020/act-public-schools-pupil-free-from-tuesday-24-march-to-school-holidays
column24: From 11.59 pm on 23 March 2020, the following non-essential businesses were required to close:  -	licensed premises  -	hotels (except for accommodation, takeaway meals, and meal delivery)  -	gyms and indoor sporting centres  -	casinos  -	entertainment venues (e.g. cinemas, nightclubs)  -	restaurants and cafes (except for takeaway or delivery)  -	places of worship (except weddings and funerals)    This represents a tightening of restrictions, as previously all non-essential businesses were allowed to remain open. This is coded as 2 because some non-essential businesses (e.g. beauty parlours, hairdressers and barbershops, swimming pools, museums, libraries) were allowed to remain open.  See http://web.archive.org/web/20220102071517/https://www.legislation.act.gov.au/View/ni/2020-169/20200323-73519/html/2020-169.html

From 11.59 pm on 25 March 2020, almost all non-essential businesses were required to close. This included a number of businesses that were allowed to remain open previously, such as swimming pools, museums and galleries, libraries, hairdressers, beauty parlours, arenas and stadiums. column77: According to the Treasury, the JobKeeper Payment became available introduced from 30 March 2020 until 27 September 2020.    The JobKeeper Payment is a payment made to eligible businesses and not-for-profits affected by the Coronavirus to support them in retaining employees. Businesses must have paid their employees before they are entitled to receive the JobKeeper payment.     Where an employee’s total remuneration is less than $1,500 per fortnight (before tax), or has been stood down, the employer must provide the employee at least $1,500 per fortnight (before tax). Where an employee earns more than $1,500 per fortnight, employers can use the payment to subsidise the employee’s wages.    Self-employed individuals will also be eligible to receive the JobKeeper payment. Self-employed individuals are not informal workers as they operate their own business with an ABN in order to be eligible to the JobKeeper Payment. Therefore, this scheme was available to formal workers.    This represents a 2F level of policy as of 27 April 2020 in Australia.    Archived link:  https://web.archive.org/web/20220304125206/https://treasury.gov.au/sites/default/files/2020-04/JobKeeper_frequently_asked_questions_2.pdf

column42: As ACT government announcement: From 11.59pm on Friday 8 May, COVID-19 restrictions have eased further to support families and our economy. These new public health directions acknowledge the impact that social isolation has on our wellbeing.  Key changes that will take effect across the ACT:  All indoor and outdoor gatherings can have a maximum of 10 people (including children).  This includes gatherings at a person’s home, which can be a maximum of 10 people (with exceptions where two households coming together results in a gathering of more than 10).  From 11.59pm Friday 15 May, restaurants and cafés and other hospitality venues are permitted to seat up to a maximum of 10 patrons at one time, while maintaining physical distancing of one person per 4 square metres and practicing good hand hygiene and frequent environmental cleaning and disinfection. This is the same for pubs and clubs offering a seated dining service.  Weddings can now have up to 10 people attend, excluding the person/s conducting the ceremony.  Indoor funerals can have up to 20 people attend, excluding the person/s conducting the service, OR outdoor funerals can have up to 30 people attend, excluding the person or persons conducting the service.  Religious ceremonies and places of worship can have up to 10 people attend, excluding the person/s conducting the service.  Outdoor bootcamps and other personal fitness training (non-contact) can be held with a maximum of 10 people, excluding the trainer. There is to be no sharing of equipment.  Real estate open houses and auctions can proceed with a maximum of 10 people, excluding staff.   Retried from  https://web.archive.org/web/20200529133045/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/protecting-yourself-and-others/groups-and-gatherings

column33: "As at 23 July 2020, there are  measures in place relating to events.   Venues are able to hold events however all venues should have a COVID safety plan and maintain physical distancing.   Records should be kept of visitors (first name, phone number, date and time) and be destroyed after 28 days  Cleaning should be heightened  and the  entry, exit and flow of visitors should be managed carefully.  For events, there are gathering rules - only 1 person for every 4 square metres or a maximum of 100 people.   There is no specific requirements for events beyond this and the expectations for businesses.   This represents a continuance of the policy and is in place across ACT. column51: "As at 23 July 2020, there are recommendations in place. People are recommended to only use transport if necessary and if they are feeling well.     They can use public transport if they are visiting in a testing centre - however you must take precautions e.g. wearing a mask, sitting in the backseat of a taxi or rideshare, maintaining physical distancing, washing hands before or after atravel, practicing good respiratory hygiene and cough etiquette.    Public transport has not changed timetables but services are different in that   '- use MyWay or pre-purchase tickets as drivers are not accepting cash  '- tap on and off each time you travel to help with COVID tracing if necessary  '- use rear doors to enter and exit buses unless you need a low front door access  '- always practise good hygiene  '- maintain physical distancing of 1.5 metres at stops and stations  '- spread out on board by leaving a seat or more if you can  '- travel outside peak times if you can.   '- drivers do not accept cash  '- front seats on buses are closed to give more space between drivers and passengers  '- light rail doors open automatically so you don’t have to touch the button  '- extra cleaning on light rail vehicles and buses and at stops and interchanges  '- extra hygiene measures for staff including personal sanitiser for drivers. column115: "As at 23 July 2020, there are restrictions on visits to high risk settings.  Residential aged care facilities will not allow any visitors unless they are a resident of the facility, an employee or contractor, part of providing goods or services, care and support, end of life support, emergency management or prospective facility.  Visitors can then be allowed in if they are there for care and support. There are no limitations to the number of hour spent. column15: By 2 June 2020, all schools in the ACT returned to face-to-face education. column24: On 23 July 2020, ACT noted that "Following advice from the ACT Chief Health Officer, the ACT will not move forward with the implementation of stage 3 restrictions in the ACT for a further two weeks. The current restrictions as outlined in the ACT’s Easing of Restrictions roadmap will stay in place and will be assessed on a weekly basis".  This means that till 10 August 2020, a range of workplace restrictions apply, including: closure of casinos and gaming in clubs; food courts (dine-in);  steam-based services, including saunas, steam rooms, steam cabinets and bathhouses; strip clubs, brothels, escort agencies; 24 hour gyms – max. 25 people when unstaffed, etc.  So the code of 2 is being given instead of 1.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200812202805/https://www.cmtedd.act.gov.au/open_government/inform/act_government_media_releases/barr/2020/further-restriction-easing-postponed-in-the-act
column33: For virtually every kind of paid activity (event), a limit of 100 applied during this period in the ACT. While the events were therefore not directly cancelled, this would have made many of them unviable - hence the code 1 -"recommend cancelling".  https://web.archive.org/web/20200807144454/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/arts-cultural-activities
column42: Home gatherings were not limited during this period: "There are no limits on visits to your home". column51: Changes from normal applied to public transport during this period, including - drivers do not accept cash, front seats on buses are closed to give more space between drivers and passengers, etc.  General recommendations applied (not mandates) during this period for people to reduce public transport use and to use masks ("if you have one"). column60: A recommendation to work from home is not a stay-at-home restriction, so even though a work from home recommendation applied during this period, this is coded as 0.  https://web.archive.org/web/20220528220903/https://www.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0011/1602695/CV_Roadmap_Recovery-plan_Ease_Restrictions_6_Aug.pdf

column88: During this period, testing was available to any symptomatic person:  those who have COVID-19 symptoms (specifically a fever of 37.5 degrees or higher or recent history of fever, and/or respiratory infection). column90: The ACT had a strong program of contact tracing in place during this period. column103: IN GENERAL NOT REQUIRED During this period, "Masks are not required in the ACT." Since there is a policy on masks, the code 0 is not appropriate. The government is also inclined to think that masks work, so they recommend under certain circumstances. Therefore coded as 1.  IN SOME CASES REQUIRED Exceptions include if you: - have COVID-like symptoms such as coughing and sneezing, and need to leave your home for an essential reason (like getting tested, seeking medical help or shopping for essential items like food or medication) - are in quarantine or self-isolation and need to leave your home for medical attention - are over 60 with underlying health problems and are unable to stay 1.5 metres away from others - have underlying health issues and are unable to stay 1.5 metres away from others.  Masks are just one line of defence against COVID-19. (This implies a recommendation)  https://web.archive.org/web/20200807205624/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/protect-yourself#Using-masks-latest-advice

column115: As of 23 March 2020, people must not visit aged care facilities unless they are any of the following: -	a resident, worker, or prospective resident at the facility -	providing goods or services essential for the facility's operation -	providing medical treatment to a resident -	providing care or support (e.g. to a family member or close friend), including end-of-life support -	there for emergency or law enforcement purposes  Even if they meet these requirements, people must not visit if they: -	have been to Victoria, Greater Sydney, COVID-19 affected areas in Queensland, or anywhere outside Australia in the past 14 days -	have been in contact with a confirmed COVID-19 case in the past 14 days -	have a fever, recent history of fever, or respiratory symptoms -	or have not been vaccinated against influenza.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200821230540/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/aged-care

column15: "As at 6 August 2020, there are measures in place  relating to education:   '- physical distancing for adults as they perceived children to be at less risk for COVID-19  - hygiene practices should be heightened with no food or drink sharing  - environmental cleaning  However, all schools are open.  This is a continuation of the policy and is in place across ACT.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200803175331/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/students-education-childcare#  https://web.archive.org/web/20200809210610/https://www.education.act.gov.au/about-us/all-news-and-news-alerts/news-items/may-2020/back-to-the-classroom  https://web.archive.org/web/20200507020819/https://www.education.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0009/1544409/CHO-advice-on-ACT-schools.pdf"
column24: "As at 6 August 2020, there are measures in place relating to businesses:  - all hospitality venues must have a COVID safety plan  '- all patrons must record the visitors who enter their place (first name and phone number, date and time of visit) and destroy records after 28 days  - physical distancing must be maintained  - manage bookings so patrons are not staying longer than two hours  - if separate indoor and outdoor spaces, maintain separate staff and separate restroom facilities  - increased cleaning   '- maintain entry, exit and flow of clients   - dancing is not permitted  '- all hospitality venues and licensed premises must display the maximum number of patrons allowed in the venue  '- casinos and adult venues are not open  - pubs, bars and clubs are allowed to serve alcohol in groups of up to 10 patrons per booking or table without  serving a meal. Patrons are to be seated    These are now all open:  - Cinemas and movie theatres  - Open air drive-in cinemas (max. 100 vehicles)  - Indoor amusement centres, arcades, outdoor and indoor play centres  - Betting agencies  - Gyms, health clubs, fitness or wellness centres, yoga, barre, pilates and spin facilities, boot camps and personal training  - Swimming pools  - Community sport and organised sporting activities  - Outdoor amusements and attractions  - Dance classes  - Choirs, bands and orchestras  - Weddings and funerals  - Personal services (beauty and nail salons, tattoo and body modification, tanning, waxing, spa and massage parlours)   - community and youth centres  - Caravan parks, campgrounds and camp sites; and   - Places of worship and religious ceremonies.   -Galleries, museums, national institutions, historic sites and libraries to allow for one person per 4 square metres throughout the venue and organised tour groups of up to 20 people (excluding staff).    This represents a continuance of the policy and is in place across ACT. There does not appear to be any variation due to vaccination status.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200716075520/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/summary-of-key-changes  https://web.archive.org/web/20200807080945/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/cafes-restaurants-and-other-hospitality  https://web.archive.org/web/20200807220501/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/casinos,-gaming-and-gambling-venues  https://web.archive.org/web/20200716075517/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/weddings-funeral-worship  https://web.archive.org/web/20200716075516/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/gyms-bootcamps-personal-training  https://web.archive.org/web/20200804091627/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/arts-cultural-activities  https://web.archive.org/web/20200716075518/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/personal-services-hairdressers-beauty-body  https://web.archive.org/web/20200807080640/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/sport-recreation-pools  https://web.archive.org/web/20200716075521/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/community-facilities  https://web.archive.org/web/20200803181814/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/adult-venues"
column33: "As at 6 August 2020, there are  measures in place relating to events.   Venues are able to hold events however all venues should have a COVID safety plan and maintain physical distancing.   Records should be kept of visitors (first name, phone number, date and time) and be destroyed after 28 days  Cleaning should be heightened  and the  entry, exit and flow of visitors should be managed carefully.  For events, there are gathering rules - only 1 person for every 4 square metres or a maximum of 100 people.   There is no specific requirements for events beyond this and the expectations for businesses.   This represents a continuance of the policy and is in place across ACT. There does not appear to be any variation due to vaccination status.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200812202805/https://www.cmtedd.act.gov.au/open_government/inform/act_government_media_releases/barr/2020/further-restriction-easing-postponed-in-the-act  https://web.archive.org/web/20200716075517/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/weddings-funeral-worship  https://web.archive.org/web/20200803180731/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/groups-and-gatherings"
column42: "As at 6 August 2020, there are  measures in place for gatherings. All indoor and outdoor gatherings are restricted to 100 people within the 1 per 4 square metre rule e.g. whatever is lower.  This includes staff for most gatherings. The exception is for hospitality venues - the maximum number of patrons excludes staff.   This represents a continuance of the policy.  https://web.archive.org/web/20220528220903/https://www.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0011/1602695/CV_Roadmap_Recovery-plan_Ease_Restrictions_6_Aug.pdf  https://web.archive.org/web/20200812202805/https://www.cmtedd.act.gov.au/open_government/inform/act_government_media_releases/barr/2020/further-restriction-easing-postponed-in-the-act  https://web.archive.org/web/20200803180731/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/groups-and-gatherings"
column51: "As at 6 August 2020, there are recommendations in place. People are recommended to only use transport if necessary and if they are feeling well.     They can use public transport if they are visiting in a testing centre - however you must take precautions e.g. wearing a mask, sitting in the backseat of a taxi or rideshare, maintaining physical distancing, washing hands before or after atravel, practicing good respiratory hygiene and cough etiquette.    Public transport has not changed timetables but services are different in that   '- use MyWay or pre-purchase tickets as drivers are not accepting cash  '- tap on and off each time you travel to help with COVID tracing if necessary  '- use rear doors to enter and exit buses unless you need a low front door access  '- always practise good hygiene  '- maintain physical distancing of 1.5 metres at stops and stations  '- spread out on board by leaving a seat or more if you can  '- travel outside peak times if you can.   '- drivers do not accept cash  '- front seats on buses are closed to give more space between drivers and passengers  '- light rail doors open automatically so you don’t have to touch the button  '- extra cleaning on light rail vehicles and buses and at stops and interchanges  '- extra hygiene measures for staff including personal sanitiser for drivers.    This is in place across ACT. This represents a continuation of the policy.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200807205148/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/transport"
column60: "As at 6 August 2020, there are no measures in place relating to stay at home. This relates to all of ACT - there is no state differentiation. This represents a continuance of the policy.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220528220903/https://www.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0011/1602695/CV_Roadmap_Recovery-plan_Ease_Restrictions_6_Aug.pdf  https://web.archive.org/web/20200812202805/https://www.cmtedd.act.gov.au/open_government/inform/act_government_media_releases/barr/2020/further-restriction-easing-postponed-in-the-act  "
column69: "As at 6 August 2020, there are  requirements for interstate travellers.   Travellers are not recommended to travel if they are unwell.   If travellers are returning from Victoria or NSW, there is a requirement to quarantine for 14 days if the spots are specific hotspots.  ACT residents cannot enter Queensland either  Quarantining must occur in a hotel or approved premises. You can quarantine for private residence, but there must be appropriate separation from other houses.    This represents a continuance of the policy.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200726125320/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/travel  https://web.archive.org/web/20200802230641/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/information-for-travellers-returning-to-the-act-from-victoria  https://web.archive.org/web/20200805193638/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/travel"
column79: "As at 6 August 2020, there are  debt relief arrangements in place.  The arrangements in place included:  - general rates bill annual increase was not applied to the 2020-2021 general rates bill. There was also a $150 rebate offered.   '- The fire and emergency service levy was frozen at the 2019-2020 level  - Quarter four residential general instalments and land tax assessments were delayed by four weeks for 2019-2020.   - there is a hardship rates deferral arrangement for household incomes which have been significantly reduced (25 % at least) by circumstances  - residential tenancy relief for landlords   - vehicle registration, parking and public transport fee increases are set at the current level  - household receiving the utilities concession will receive an additional $200 rebate  '- a fund will be set up for electricity costs (up to $250,000)  - the utilities network facilities tax is frozen at the current level passing on savings to customers  This represents a continuance of the policy across ACT.    https://web.archive.org/web/20200811005946/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/business-and-work/economic-survival-package/families-and-households"
column86: "As at 6 August 2020, there is a coordinated public information campaign (including a website, call centres and social media).   https://web.archive.org/web/20200811005945/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/signs-and-factsheets  https://web.archive.org/web/20200806000554/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/updates/confirmed-case-information"
column88: "As at 6 August 2020, the following people are recommended to get a COVID-19 test: those who have COVID-19 symptoms (specifically a fever of 37.5 degrees or higher or recent history of fever, and respiratory infection), those who are a close contact or during outbreaks in high-risk settings or as part of public health investigations where the source of a person's exposure to COVID-19 is uncertain.   It represents a continuance of the policy. This applies across ACT.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200805191515/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/symptoms-and-getting-tested"
column90: "As of 6 August 2020, the ACT Government is recording statistics relating to the number of COVID cases. This includes also where the current cases are located. This is updated regularly. There is also contact tracing in that close contacts are contacted. This represents a continuance of the policy.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200806000554/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/updates/confirmed-case-information"
column103: "As at 6 August 2020, face masks are not required unless an individual has COVID-19 or suspects that they have COVID-19.It also includes if you are in quaratine or self-isolation, over 60 with underlying health issues or under 60 with underlying health issues and unable to physically distance.  They must then wear a mask in public transport or other places on the way to testing.   This is a continuance of the policy. column106: "As at 6 August 2020, the vaccine is not available to any age groups. This represents a continuation of the policy and is in place across ACT.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200805203950/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/protect-yourself"

column74: As published on the Department of Home Affairs website on operation direction, response to Novel Coronavirus on pdf document that foreign nationals who do not meet the travel exemption categories are not be allowed to enter Australia. This travel ban came into effect from 20 March 2020 at 2100 AEDST.   All travellers arriving in Australia are required to undertake the mandatory 14 day quarantine period at designated facilities in accordance with applicable State or Territory legislation. This came into effect from 28 March 2020 at 23:59hrs AEDST.   This represents a continuation of the policy response.  https://web.archive.org/web/20210416125022/https://www.homeaffairs.gov.au/foi/files/2020/fa-200700310-document-released.PDF
column77: Median weekly earnings were $1,209.00 for all employees, and the JobKeeper Payment was greater than 50% median salary.  The JobKeeper Payment helps businesses significantly impacted by the Coronavirus cover the costs of their employees’ wages, so more Australians can retain their jobs and continue to earn an income. Employers will notify employees if they are claiming the fortnightly payment of $1,500. The first payments were made in the week commencing 4 May 2020.  Since 27 April 2020 the Government has temporarily expanded eligibility to income support payments and established a new, time-limited Coronavirus supplement to be paid at a rate of $550 per fortnight. This is paid to both existing and new recipients of Jobseeker Payment, Youth Allowance, Parenting Payment, Austudy, ABSTUDY Living Allowance, Farm Household Allowance and Special Benefit. The Government is also temporarily expanding access for the JobSeeker Payment by relaxing the partner income test.  This represents continuation in the COVID-19 policy response.   https://web.archive.org/web/20210714153920/https://treasury.gov.au/sites/default/files/2020-07/Fact_sheet-Income_Support_for_Individuals.pdf  https://web.archive.org/web/20220331122605/https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/labour/earnings-and-working-conditions/employee-earnings-and-hours-australia/may-2021

column15: Public schools in the ACT are open. Most students and teachers have returned to school. However, students and teachers with chronic health conditions or compromised immune systems can work or study from home.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200817070833/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/students-education-childcare
column24: From 10 August 2020, stage 3 of the ACT Recovery Plan has begun. Businesses such as cinemas, saunas, food-courts, and 24 hour gyms are allowed to reopen. However, there are still restrictions. For example, there is a capacity limit of 25 people when unstaffed. There is a 1 person per 4 square meter rule.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200919094434/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/canberra-recovery
column33: Public events are allowed. However, social distancing guidelines might be adhered to. Indoor spaces must be large enough to allow for one person for every 4 square metres of space. Events such as community sports, weddings, funerals, and religious ceremonies are permitted.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200716075517/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions/weddings-funeral-worship
column42: Public gatherings have a limit of one person per 4 square metres for indoor or outdoor spaces, up to 100 people. There are no limits on home visits.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200817070932/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/groups-and-gatherings
column51: There are currently no changes to timetables, but there are measures to prevent the spread of COVID-19. There is mandatory cashless payments. Passengers must use of rear doors to enter and exit public transport. There is also extra cleaning on light rail vehicles and buses and at stops and interchanges, and extra hygiene measures for staff including personal sanitiser for drivers.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200817070913/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/transport
column60: There are no stay-at-home requirements in the ACT. Public transport and businesses are in operation, despite some restrictions.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200817070839/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/what-you-can-do/faqs-changes-to-restrictions
column69: There are COVID-affected areas in New South Wales (NSW) and Victoria (VIC) which are impacting travel into and out of the Australian Capital Territory (ACT). Travellers from Victoria, who must be ACT-residents, must enter a 14-day quarantine. Travellers from NSW should quarantine if they returned from a high-risk area.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200817070928/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/travel
column79: The ACT government has offered broad debt/contract relief in areas such as residential rates, tenancy relief, stamp duty concessions, a freezing of all 2020-21 vehicle registration, parking and public transport fee. Furthermore, households already receiving the utilities concession will receive an additional $200 rebate through their electricity bill. The Utilities Network Facilities Tax is also frozen.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200716075648/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/business-and-work/economic-survival-package/families-and-households
column86: The ACT government has a dedicated website for the pandemic. It maintains a series of social media profiles, on which it posts information on the pandemic.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200813/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/home
column88: Anyone exhibiting symptoms of COVID, no matter how mild, is eligible for a test.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200813063943/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/symptoms-and-getting-tested
column90: The ACT government regularly publishes statistics on the pandemic such as daily cases, tests conducted, etc. The list of confirmed cases is constantly being updated.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200811005948/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/updates/confirmed-case-information
column103: Masks are not required in the ACT. The health advice remains that where there is no community transmission of COVID-19, masks are not required.   Exceptions include symptomatic/quarantining individuals who need to leave for an essential reason. People over 60 with underlying health problems and are unable to stay 1.5 metres away from others should wear a mask. Furthermore, people who have underlying health issues and are unable to stay 1.5 metres away from others should also use a mask.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200811005938/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/protect-yourself
column106: COVID-19 vaccines were not yet available at this time. The ACT's vaccination rollout began on February 22, 2021     https://web.archive.org/web/20210515021544/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/vaccine/when-will-i-get-the-covid-19-vaccine

column74: As of 15 Aug 2020, Australia’s international border remains closed, since the Australian Government closed the border to all but non-citizens and non-residents on 20 March 2020.    This represents a continuation of the policy of significant change to pre-covid times as of 15 Sep 2020.    Archived link:  https://web.archive.org/web/20210416125022/https://www.homeaffairs.gov.au/foi/files/2020/fa-200700310-document-released.PDF
column77: On 22 March (this is a continuation of the existing policy), the National government introduces economic support packages in response to the covid-19 pandemic which includes support for workers and households.   The Government is temporarily expanding eligibility to income support payments and establishing a new, time-limited Coronavirus supplement to be paid at a rate of $550 per fortnight for the next 6 months (until September).   https://web.archive.org/web/20220517043637/https://www.pm.gov.au/media/supporting-australian-workers-and-business     Also, there continues to be income support available across Australia, replacing >50% of lost income for formal workers. column15: ACT public schools have returned to face-to-face instruction, with remote options available for students vulnerable to COVID-19. However, camps, interstate excursions, large gatherings of more than 100 people, discos and celebrations, and in-person fundraisers involving adults have been cancelled. Small scheduled events, such as one-on-one parent-teacher interviews and small assemblies of less than 100 people, may continue. Schools are instructed to keep records of all visitors to assist potential contact tracing.  This is a continuation of policy since July 2020; see https://web.archive.org/web/20220611110836/https://www.education.act.gov.au/about-us/all-news-and-news-alerts/news-items/july-2020/updated-information-on-covid-19-health-directions-and-restrictions-for-act-public-schools.
column24: The ACT moved to stage 3.1 of its recovery roadmap on 10 August 2020. Some additional categories of businesses (e.g. casinos, food courts, saunas, strip clubs, brothels, and 24-hour gyms) were allowed to reopen; following this easing of restrictions, only high-risk businesses (e.g. nightclubs) were required to remain closed. Non-essential businesses may host up to 100 people, provided that social distancing of 1 person per 4 square metres is maintained and a COVID-19 safety plan is followed. Employees are encouraged to work from home when this is possible. See https://web.archive.org/web/20210226110338/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0007/1610944/CV_Roadmap_Recovery-plan_Ease_Restrictions_20August20.pdf.
column33: Large events of more than 100 people are not permitted. Smaller events may continue provided that social distancing of 1 person per 4 square metres is maintained. For gatherings conducted at a "non-essential business or undertaking" (which includes religious services, weddings and funerals, conferences and conventions, public performances, sporting events and cinemas) event organisers are also required to follow a COVID-19 safety plan and keep records of attendees to assist contact tracing.   This is a continuation of previous policy since at least June 2020. See Phase 3.1 of the COVID-19 Recovery Plan: https://web.archive.org/web/20210627101158/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0006/1629330/PICC0050-COVID-Recovery-Plan.pdf   and Restricted Activities Direction No. 7: http://web.archive.org/web/20220622095330/https://www.legislation.act.gov.au/View/ni/2020-484/20200812-74810/html/2020-484.html
column42: Gatherings are limited to 100 people, or 1 person per 4 square metres, whichever is lesser. Gatherings regarded to be essential (e.g. gatherings necessary for normal operations of a workplace, shopping centre, health care facility, airport, school, or legislative body; gatherings for emergency or law enforcement purposes; gatherings for the purpose of private or public transportation) are excepted from restrictions. This is a continuation of policy since at least 12 August 2020, see http://web.archive.org/web/20220622095330/https://www.legislation.act.gov.au/View/ni/2020-484/20200812-74810/html/2020-484.html
column51: Public transport continues to operate and timetables are unchanged, but people are encouraged to use private transport if they can, and avoid public transport if they are feeling unwell.     A number of other precautionary measures have also been implemented:  -	Cash payments of fares are no longer accepted  -	Front seats of buses are closed off to ensure social distancing between passengers and the driver  -	Light rail doors open automatically, so passengers don't need to push the button  -	Additional hygiene measures (e.g. hand sanitizer for drivers, additional cleaning).  -	Passengers are advised to maintain social distancing, and travel outside peak hours.    See https://web.archive.org/web/20200901054233/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/transport.
column60: As of August 20, 2020, the ACT is in stage 3.1 of its roadmap to recovery (see https://web.archive.org/web/20210226110338/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0007/1610944/CV_Roadmap_Recovery-plan_Ease_Restrictions_20August20.pdf). Given that most non-essential businesses were permitted to open, it can be assumed there were no stay-at-home orders at this time.
column69: As of August 20, 2020, travellers from Victoria who are not residents in the ACT are not permitted to enter the ACT, unless they have been granted an exemption by ACT Health. ACT residents may return home from Victoria, but must quarantine for 14 days since they were last in Victoria. Travellers from elsewhere in Australia are not required to quarantine, but are advised to avoid high-risk settings if they have visited Greater Sydney or other COVID-19 affected areas. ACT residents are advised not to travel outside the ACT unless it is essential, but are not forbidden from doing so. This is a continuation of previous policy, aside from the recent removal of Newcastle from the list of COVID-19 affected areas.  See https://web.archive.org/web/20200826011420/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/travel.
column79: A range of measures to protect tenants and landlords affected by COVID-19 were in place for six months beginning on 22 April 2020. This included a moratorium on evictions for tenants unable to pay rent as a result of COVID-19 impacts. Landlords are also prohibited from increasing rent for households impacted by COVID-19. See https://web.archive.org/web/20201023000436/https://www.justice.act.gov.au/safer-communities/protection-rights/information-tenants-and-occupants-impacted-covid-19
column86: The ACT Government runs a public information campaign through multiple channels. column88: ACT Health advises people to get tested if they have a fever of 37.5 degrees or higher, or have respiratory symptoms, while people with other symptoms may get tested after consulting with a doctor. column90: There was no community transmission of COVID-19 at this time, so no contact tracing took place in practice. column103: There was no community transmission of COVID-19 in the ACT at this time, and healthy people were not required or recommended to wear masks. column24: According to the ACT government's recovery plan for easing COVID-19 restrictions, during this time period, although there was still a 1 person per 4 square meters restriction and 100 person limit imposed, various businesses were now allowed to reopen as of Phase 3.1 such as:  -casinos and gaming in clubs  -food courts (dine in)  -steam based services  -strip clubs, brothels, escort services  -24 hour gyms    However, apart from these and businesses allowed to reopen during Stage 2, employees were still expected to work from home if possible so some sectors remained closed. column33: During this time period, the ACT Easing of Restrictions Roadmap would have been at Phase 3.1 where although gatherings weren't forbidden, there was a 100 person cap limit (excluding on premise staff) and 1 person for every 4 square metres cap. column51: During this time period, individuals are heavily recommended to only use public transport if they are feeling well. column60: During this time period, there were no mandates from the ACT government for individuals to remain at home unless they were infected by COVID-19 and were a close contact, where they had to self-isolate. column69: During this time period, there were restrictions with travel to NSW and Victoria from the ACT. column86: During this time period, the ACT government had set up a coordinated public campaign for COVID-19, with a regularly updated website containing latest case numbers and any changes to government policies as well as social media pages and a helpline. column88: During this time period, any individual who displayed symptoms of COVID-19 (involving fever of 37.5 degrees or higher and/or a respiratory infection) were suggested to take a COVID-19 test. column115: During this time period, the ACT government mandated that all individuals are not allowed to enter or remain on the premises of a residential aged care facilities unless:  -they are a resident  -they are an employee or contractor of the aged care facility  -person's presence is required for providing goods or services necessary for the operation of the facility  -person's presence is required for providing health, medical or pharmaceutical goods or services to a resident  -person's presence is for a care and support visit to a resident  -person's presence is for end of life support for resident  -they are prospective resident  -person's presence is required for emergency management or law enforcement    However, any person who has returned from overseas in the last 14 days, been in Victoria, Greater Sydney or COVID-affected areas of Queensland in the past 14 days, been in the contact of a confirmed COVID-19 case in the last 14 days, not have had 2020 influenza vaccine or has temperature higher than 37.5 degrees or symptoms of respiratory infection cannot enter aged care facilities at all.    No school or childcare groups are allowed to visit but children of all ages are allowed to, given they have received the 2020 influenza vaccine (exempting babies under 6 months) and follow restrictions during their visit. No more than two people can visit a resident at any time. These are considered extensive protections due to the heavy restrictions on individuals placed.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200901054307/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/aged-care

column79: A range of debt/contract relief has been provided by the ACT government for financially struggling individuals. First, the usual annual increase has not been applied to 2020-21 general rates bills and a $150 AUD ($110 USD) rebate has been provided to the fixed charge component of all general rates bills.    The Fire and Emergency Services Levy in 2020-21 has also been frozen at the 2019-20 level while the 2019-20 quarter 4 residential general instalments and land tax assessments has been delayed by 4 weeks and the 2020-21 quarter 1 residential general instalments and land tax assessments by 3 weeks.    Rates deferrals for owner occupiers experiencing hardship due to COVID-19 also can be deferred without interest for 12 months as long as income has been reduced by at least 25% due to unemployment, reduction in hours or loss of small business income. Land tax and rates rebates are also offered for landlords who reduce rent by at least 25% for tenants impacted by COVID-19 which is equal to 50% of rent reduction. Stamp duty concessions are also offered for some home buyers planning to live in their new property and households already receiving the Utilities Concession will receive an additional $200 AUD ($147 USD) rebate through their electricity bill.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200901054241/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/business-and-work/economic-survival-package/families-and-households

column51: Public transport continues to operate and timetables are unchanged, but people are encouraged to use private transport if they can, and avoid public transport if they are feeling unwell. column15: According to the ACT Government’s website (updated on 24 Aug 2020; archived on 18 Sep 2020), ACT public schools are open. Most students and teachers have returned to school. Students and teachers with chronic health conditions or compromised immune systems can work or study from home. See also: para 21(o) of the Public Health (Restricted Activities – Gatherings, Business or Undertakings) Emergency Direction 2020 (No 9) (ACT) (effective from 9 Sep 2020, 9:00 am to 17 Sep 2020), attending schools was allowed (i.e. a group of 2 or more people occupying a single usable indoor space or usable outdoor space at the same time).    From term 3 (Monday 20 Jul to Friday 25 Sep), schools can welcome back our families for scheduled events such as parent-teacher interviews and small assemblies with physical distancing and hygiene measures in place. Schools will continue to limit the number of adults on school grounds, however, where scheduled events are planned (such as one-on-one parent-teacher interviews and small assemblies of less than 100 people) parents can attend the school. Records will be kept of visitors entering the school so contact tracing can occur if required.    This represents a 1G level of policy in the ACT as of 11 Sep 2020.    Archived link:  https://web.archive.org/web/20200918150845/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/students-education-childcare#    https://web.archive.org/web/20220621144648/https://www.legislation.act.gov.au/View/ni/2020-592/20200909-75163/html/2020-592.html    https://web.archive.org/web/20220302163238/https://www.education.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0007/801583/Term-Date-2019-2025.pdf    https://web.archive.org/web/20220303100616/https://www.education.act.gov.au/about-us/all-news-and-news-alerts/news-items/june-2020/covid-19-and-school-arrangements-for-term-3-2020
column33: According to the Public Health (Restricted Activities – Gatherings, Business or Undertakings) Emergency Direction 2020 (No 9) (ACT) (effective from 9 Sep 2020, 9:00 am to 17 Sep 2020), ‘public events’ were generally categorised as ‘non-essential business or undertaking’ in part 1 para 23. In part 1 para 3, a person who owns, controls or operates a non-essential business or undertaking in the ACT must comply with the requirements for a non-essential business or undertaking in this Direction.  This person must:  a.	develop and adhere to a COVID-19 Safety Plan, and produce the plan when requested by an authorised person; and  b.	display a sign specifying the maximum occupancy under this Direction of that business; and  c.	for contact tracing purposes, ask that each person who attends the business or undertaking record their attendance at the business or premises by either: (i) using the Check In CBR app; or (ii) providing a first name and contact phone number, and if provided, keep a record of those details, together with the date and time at which the person attended and produce the record if requested by an authorised person.    Each gathering (i.e. a group of 2 or more people occupying a single usable indoor space or usable outdoor space at the same time) in premises from where a non-essential business or undertaking operates must not exceed 1 person per 4 square metres or the maximum person limit (excluding a worker) per usable space in the premises (whichever is the lesser), subject to exceptions.    Part 1 para 23 sets out additional requirements for attending non-essential businesses or undertakings.    For example:  Gallery/museum (23(i))  -	the maximum person limit does not apply; and  -	if attending a tour, it cannot be more than 20 people, and the duration should be no more than 2 hours    It also suggested the followings (Attachment A):  -	In a given occupied space, there be a density of no more than 1 person per 4 square metres or the maximum person limit of usable space (whichever is the lesser), and this should take into account objects and items that may impact the total free space;  -	Hand hygiene products and suitable waste receptacles should be available, to allow for frequent cleaning and waste disposal;  -	Physical distancing of at least 1.5 metres between people, and physical contact should be avoided wherever possible;  -	The occupancy allowance should be displayed at the entrance of each venue or space;  -	The recommendations for unwell individuals to isolate at home and not attend published by the Commonwealth Department of Health should be promoted and displayed prominently so that they can be seen and read easily by a person at or near an entrance to the indoor space;  -	For settings where there is ongoing movement and an increased number of interactions between people (for example food markets) and an individual’s attendance is not in the course of their employment at the place, an individual’s attendance should be less than 2 hours duration;  -	Where activities involve the use of equipment, that equipment should be regularly cleaned and, where practicable, not be shared by people other than members of the same household.    This represents a 1G level of policy in the ACT as of 11 Sep 2020.    Archived link:  https://web.archive.org/web/20220621144648/https://www.legislation.act.gov.au/View/ni/2020-592/20200909-75163/html/2020-592.html

column88: The ACT Government’s website (updated on 10 Sep 2020; archived on 18 Sep 2020) suggested that people can get tested for COVID-19 if they have:  -	a fever of 37.5 degrees or higher (or recent history of fever such as chills or night sweats)  -	and/or a respiratory infection, such as shortness of breath, cough or sore throat.    If people have other symptoms, they may be eligible for testing after they see a health professional. If people have no symptoms and have not attended a COVID-19 affected area, they don’t need to be tested.    This represents a 2 level of policy in the ACT as of 11 Sep 2020.    Archived link:  https://web.archive.org/web/20200918150803/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/symptoms-and-getting-tested
column90: The ACT Government’s website (published on 9 Sep 2020) suggested that enabled individuals to check in to venues and have this data stored securely with ACT Health in the event contact tracing is needed due to a confirmed case of COVID-19 in the community. The ACT Health contact tracing would use the Check in CBR app to identify and assist anyone who may have been exposed to COVID-19 as of 11 Sep 2020.    Additionally, the Department of Health (Commonwealth) suggested that ACT Health had also offered to share the app with other states and territories to support their contact tracing capabilities.    This represents a 2 level of policy in the ACT as of 11 Sep 2020.    Archived link:  https://web.archive.org/web/20201205171352/https://www.act.gov.au/our-canberra/latest-news/2020/september/check-out-the-new-check-in-cbr-app    https://web.archive.org/web/20201119211131/https://www.health.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2020/11/national-contact-tracing-review-national-contact-tracing-review.pdf
column103: The ACT Government’s website (updated on 10 Sep 2020; 18 Sep 2020) suggested that masks were not required in the ACT where there is no community transmission of COVID-19 as of 11 Sep 2020.    Exceptions include if people:  -	have COVID-like symptoms such as coughing and sneezing, and need to leave your home for an essential reason (like getting tested, seeking medical help or shopping for essential items like food or medication)  -	are in quarantine or self-isolation and need to leave your home for medical attention  -	are over 60 with underlying health problems and are unable to stay 1.5 metres away from others  -	have underlying health issues and are unable to stay 1.5 metres away from others.    Masks were just one line of defence against COVID-19. The best defences for the ACT continued to be physical distancing, hand and respiratory hygiene, staying at home if people were unwell, and getting tested if they had symptoms.    This represents a 1G level of policy in the ACT as of 11 Sep 2020.    See also: Face mask guidance in the ACT (http://web.archive.org/web/20200929135845/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0004/1618816/Face-Mask-Guide.pdf)    Archived link:  http://web.archive.org/web/20200918150820/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/protect-yourself#Using-masks-latest-advice
column106: As of 11 Sep 2020, there continues to be no availability of COVID-19 vaccines in the ACT, as the Australian Government commenced the vaccine roll-out on 22 February 2021.    This represents a 0 level of policy as of 11 Sep 2020 in the ACT.    Archived link:  https://web.archive.org/web/20210218072330/https://www.health.gov.au/news/covid-19-vaccine-rollout-on-track-to-begin-22-february

column115: During this time period, continuing from previous policy, various restrictions are placed on aged care facilities for the protection of the elderly. Individuals cannot enter or remain on the premises of an aged care facility unless the person is a resident, employee or contractor of the facility, the person's presence is required for purposes of providing essential goods or services for operation of the facility, providing health, medical or pharmaceutical goods or services to a resident, a care and support visit for resident, end of life support for resident, required for emergency management or law enforcement or the person is there as prospective resident of facility.     Only two visitors are allowed for a resident at any time although the number of hours is not restricted. The visit must be kept to a resident's room, outdoors or specific areas designated for visits. Physical distancing must also be practiced and any children must be supervised. However, if an individual has returned from overseas in past 14 days, been in Victoria, Greater Sydney or COVID-19 affected areas of Queensland in past 14 days, been in contact with confirmed COVID-19 case in past 14 days, have temperature higher than 37.5 degrees or history of fever or has symptoms of a respiratory infection or have not received 2020 flu vaccination and does not have a documented medical contraindication, they will not be allowed to enter the facility (whether as visitor or worker).    External excursions for groups of residents are not permitted, only to attend small family gatherings in line with government limits where a risk assessment should be conducted for each visit.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200918150903/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/aged-care

column74: As of 15 Sep 2020, Australia’s international border remains closed, since the Australian Government closed the border to all but non-citizens and non-residents on 20 March 2020.    This represents a continuation of the policy of significant change to pre-covid times as of 15 Sep 2020.    Archived link:  https://web.archive.org/web/20210416125022/https://www.homeaffairs.gov.au/foi/files/2020/fa-200700310-document-released.PDF

column15: Continuing from previous policy, all schools remain open during this time with most students and teachers having returned to school. However, some students who have chronic health conditions or compromised immune systems are still allowed to work or study from home. Large gatherings such as assemblies are slowly being reintroduced with various physical distancing and hygiene restrictions but the number of adults allowed into the school is still capped with records of visitors being kept to allow for contact tracing.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200918150845/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/students-education-childcare
column24: During this time period, the ACT was at Step 3.1 of the government's 'COVID-19 Easing of Restrictions Roadmap' where casinos and gaming in clubs, dine in food courts, steam based services, strip clubs and brothels and 24 hour gyms (max 25 people when unstaffed) were allowed to reopen. For these businesses, working from home was voluntary however, several sectors still at the time remained closed. From 18 September, smaller sized venues, facilities and businesses were allowed to return to pre-COVID capacity with maximum of 25 people (excluding staff) in the venue. All open businesses had to have a COVID-19 Safety Plan, a density limit of 1 person per 4 square metres and an absolute max of 100 people for each indoor and outdoor space.  Source:  https://web.archive.org/web/20210627101158/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0006/1629330/PICC0050-COVID-Recovery-Plan.pdf
column33: Under the 'Public Health (Restricted Activities - Gatherings, Business or Undertakings) Emergency Direction 2020 (No. 9)', various restrictions are placed on public gatherings for the event to be allowed to take place.    For non-essential events, a density limit of 1 person per 4 square meters is applied with a maximum limit of 100 people, a COVID-19 plan must be developed and adhered to and all people attending the business or undertaking must record their attendance through the Check in CBR app or a physical record.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20220621144648/https://www.legislation.act.gov.au/View/ni/2020-592/20200909-75163/html/2020-592.html (active from 9 September 2020)
column42: During this time period, all public gatherings were restricted to at most 100 people with a density limit of one person per 4 square meters. There are, however, no limits with gatherings at home. Physical distancing of 1.5 meters and good hygiene is also recommended.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200918150901/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/groups-and-gatherings
column51: Individuals who are unwell or in quarantine or isolation are heavily suggested not to take public transport anywhere, instead using private transport. People in quarantine who need to ride public transport to get tested are allowed to use public transport as long as they wear a mask, sit at the back and maintain physical distance with other passengers. Public transport during this time doesn't accept cash, only MyWay or pre-purchased tickets and people are suggested to tap on and off to help wth contact tracing. Physical distancing and good hygiene practices is also emphasised.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200918150757/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/transport
column60: As seen in the ACT government's 'Canberra Recovery Plan: Easing of Restrictions', during this time period, public gatherings were allowed to occur and businesses were allowed to reopen. Thus, there were no particular requirements for individuals to stay at home, barr if they were found as a close contact or case.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200918150833/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/canberra-recovery
column79: https://web.archive.org/web/20200918150838/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/business-and-work/economic-survival-package/families-and-households
column86: During this time period, the Canberran government continues to maintain a coordinated public campaign against COVID-19 with a regularly updated website containing daily case numbers, updates on health policy from the government and various advice on how to protect oneself against COVID-19. A COVID-19 helpline is also available to call from 8am-8pm daily as well as a variety of social media accounts with regular posts.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200918152527/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/
column88: During this time period, continuing from previous policy, getting tested for COVID-19 was suggested for all individuals displaying a fever over 37.5 degrees or a respiratory infection, such as a sore throat or cough. Other circumstances might also cause individuals to be recommended for testing, including for people in quarantine who might have been exposed to COVID-19, during outbreaks in high-risk facilities or as part of public health investigations.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200918150803/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/symptoms-and-getting-tested
column90: During this time period, the ACT government continues to have comprehensive contact tracing with continuous updates to any cases of COVID-19 occurring on public transport or flights for the public to know as well as daily case numbers. Also, starting in September, the Check In CBR app has been made available to the general public allowing individuals to sign in whenever they enter a venue. The places any confirmed case visits is thus recorded and used to notify of any potential contacts.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200919094300/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/updates/confirmed-case-information  https://web.archive.org/web/20201205171352/https://www.act.gov.au/our-canberra/latest-news/2020/september/check-out-the-new-check-in-cbr-app
column103: During this time period, although masks were not required to be worn by the ACT government, they were recommended as a line of protection against COVID-19 along with physical distancing and good hygiene. Exceptions to this include having COVID-19 symptoms such as coughing and needing to leave home for an essential reason (e.g. getting tested, shopping for essential items), in quarantine or self-isolation and need to leave home for medical attention or have underlying health issues and cannot stay 1.5 meters from others.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200918150820/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/protect-yourself
column106: During this time period, no COVID-19 vaccines had yet been approved by the Canberran government for public use and thus a vaccination policy didn't exist. The earliest mention of vaccines being approved for use came in mid-January 2021 where a vaccination strategy program was due to start being implemented from mid-late February 2021.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20210119003350/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/stay-safe-and-healthy/covid-19-vaccine

column60: Under step 3.1 of Canberra's recovery plan, there are no stay-at-home requirements.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200929073500/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/canberra-recovery
column69: As of September 2020, travellers from Victoria who are not residents in the ACT are not permitted to enter the ACT, unless they have been granted an exemption by ACT Health. ACT residents may return home from Victoria, but must quarantine for 14 days since they were last in Victoria. Travellers from elsewhere in Australia are not required to quarantine, but are advised to avoid high-risk settings if they have visited COVID-19 affected areas in New South Wales or Queensland. ACT residents are advised not to travel outside the ACT unless it is essential, but are not forbidden from doing so. See https://web.archive.org/web/20200924022250/https://www.covid19.act.gov.au/community/travel

They can use public transport if they are visiting in a testing centre - however you must take precautions e.g. wearing a mask, sitting in the backseat of a taxi or rideshare, maintaining physical distancing, washing hands before or after atravel, practicing good respiratory hygiene and cough etiquette. column15: In line with the broader community easing of restrictions, up to 200 parents and family members will now be allowed to attend graduation ceremonies on school sites.    While schools will make their own decisions on how events will best operate for their school community, ACT public school graduation ceremonies will generally take place on school grounds, with up to two adults attending per student where possible.    Schools with larger groups of graduating students may need to split sessions or limit family attendance to one adult per student. column42: Gathering in a public place is limited to two people.  There are certain exceptions to this rule, including for a gathering: for work of residents from the same household for a wedding (limited to a total of 5 people including the person conducting the service) for a funeral (limited to a total of 10 people, not including the staff preparing and conducting the service e.g. funeral director) to move into a new home or business premises to provide care or assistance to a vulnerable person to provide emergency assistance to fulfil a legal obligation including attending a court or tribunal, satisfying bail requirements or participating in legal proceedings). column115: Staff and visitors who have travelled overseas or who have had contact with a confirmed case must not attend the facility for 14 days from the time they returned from overseas or last had contact with a case.     A RACF is a resident’s home, and all NSW residents are prohibited under the Public Health (COVID-19 Restrictions on Gathering and Movement) Order 2020, from leaving their home unless for a reasonable excuse. The four main reasonable excuses are:  -obtaining food or other goods and services  -travelling for the purposes of work or education if the person cannot do it at home  -exercise  -medical or caring reasons.    In addition, Commonwealth and State and Territory bodies have jointly advised:  -no external excursions for residents should currently be permitted (17 March - Australian Health Protection Principal Committee)  -that those over the age of 70 (or over 60 for those with existing health conditions or co-morbidities, or over 50 for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders) should self-isolate at home to the maximum extent practicable (29 March - National Cabinet).    This is a continuation of the previous policy.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200504062101/https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/Infectious/covid-19/Pages/aged-care-faq.aspx

A RACF is a resident’s home, and all NSW residents are prohibited under the Public Health (COVID-19 Restrictions on Gathering and Movement) Order 2020, from leaving their home unless for a reasonable excuse. column74: International Travel Restrictions    The National Cabinet noted the AHPPC’s advice on high-risk countries for COVID-19 importation risk and its continued support for the 14 day self isolation requirement for all returning travellers.  The National Cabinet welcomed the Commonwealth Government’s decision to stop the entry of non-citizens and non-permanent residents and their immediate families into Australia after 9pm AEDT on Friday 20 March 2020 in order to align international travel restrictions with the risks. Limited exemptions will be available under the authority of the Australian Border Force Commissioner, focused on individuals providing critical or essential services or on compassionate grounds.    Archived link: http://web.archive.org/web/20230213192259/https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22media%2Fpressrel%2F7255924%22
column77: Continuation of policy from Mar 22, 2020 where the Australian Government announced a second economic support package, bringing additional support of around $66 billion. The additional measures included:    Support for workers and households through the coronavirus supplement of $550 per fortnight that would be paid to ‘both existing and new recipients of the JobSeeker Payment, Youth Allowance jobseeker, Parenting Payment, Farm Household Allowance and Special Benefit’ support to households through a second $750 payment to social security and veteran income support recipients and eligible concession card holders  "Additional announcement on Mar 30, 2020 of The JobKeeper Payment  which is a subsidy to businesses, which will keep more Australians in jobs through the course of the coronavirus outbreak.    The payment will be paid to employers, for up to six months, for each eligible employee that was on their books on 1 March 2020 and is retained or continues to be engaged by that employer.    Where a business has stood down employees since 1 March, the payment will help them maintain connection with their employees.    Employers will receive a payment of $1,500 per fortnight per eligible employee. Every eligible employee must receive at least $1,500 per fortnight from this business, before tax."    Archived link: http://web.archive.org/web/20230213194347/https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22media%2Fpressrel%2F7255979%22    Archived link: http://web.archive.org/web/20230213194845/https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22media%2Fpressrel%2F7269587%22

column77: 1. The Government’s JobKeeper Payment helped keep more Australians in jobs and support businesses affected by the significant economic impact of the coronavirus. column15: According to the NSW Government (updated on 12 June 2020), schools in NSW are operating full time, and many additional activities are now able to recommence. All schools have returned to full-time on-campus learning. Students do not need to follow strict adult physical distancing guidelines, but should follow good hygiene practices like:  -regularly washing hands  -avoiding sharing drinks or food  -coughing or sneezing into your elbow, or a tissue which should be discarded immediately  -filling water bottles from bubblers rather than using the bubbler directly.    Additionally, the physical distancing of children in schools is not required under the Australian HPPC guidelines. Research has shown limited transmission risk associated with school children in the school environment. All adults must maintain physical distance from each other (1.5m) including teachers and support staff, and parents.    Schools will continue to receive additional cleaning in line with the AHPPC guidelines and advice from NSW Health. Target areas include high-touch areas and other hard surfaces, door handles, lockers, light switches and handrails in stairways and movement areas. There will also be additional cleaning of toilets and bubblers and topping up of supplies like soap.    This represents a continuation of the policy of significant changes to pre-covid times.    Archived link: https://web.archive.org/web/20200703174458/https://education.nsw.gov.au/covid-19/advice-for-families

column33: According to the NSW Government website as of 29 July 2020, all food and drink premises, bars, registered clubs, and casinos were required to follow the same restrictions as pubs from 12:01am on 24 July 2020 onwards.
