column15: As of 30 November 2020, schools in Queensland have resumed normal attendance except for in cases where medical advice supports a student or staff to be at home or absent, then learning from home practices will be implemented. Otherwise, any students not attending school will be marked per usual absence policies. Camps and excursions are still restricted to locations or businesses with an approved COVID-19 Safe Industry Plan or else having taken all measures to meet departmental and CHO requirements. Musical performances are also restricted where all individuals must be socially distanced, wind instrument players should have a spit rag and practices should preferably be done outside. Hygiene practices are also strongly suggested by the government.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201130014209/https://qed.qld.gov.au/about-us/news-and-media/novel-coronavirus/covid-19-operating-guidelines-for-queensland-state-schools
column24: As of 26 November 2020, the state government has allowed businesses to reopen but only under a variety of conditions. Businesses must abide by occupant density, have a COVID Safe Approved Plan or Checklist, collect and keep information about all guests, patrons and staff unless otherwise specified. Self-service buffets are also still banned as well as indoor dancing spaces.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20211005033737/https://www.health.qld.gov.au/system-governance/legislation/cho-public-health-directions-under-expanded-public-health-act-powers/revoked/business-activity-undertaking-direction-10
column33: Under the state government's "Restrictions on Businesses, Activities and Undertakings Direction (No.10)", beginning from 26 November 2020, most public events were allowed to take place as long as they abided conditions placed by the government, including keeping all contact information of customers, patrons and staff as well as abiding by occupancy densities and having an Approved Plan or Checklist. Indoor dancing spaces and self-service buffets continue to be banned.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20211005033737/https://www.health.qld.gov.au/system-governance/legislation/cho-public-health-directions-under-expanded-public-health-act-powers/revoked/business-activity-undertaking-direction-10
column42: By the "Movement and Gathering Direction (No.6)" , from 16 November 2020, caps on the number of people allowed to attend gatherings depend on whether the area is restricted or non-restricted, which can be found on the Queensland government website. For non-restricted areas, the maximum people allowed is 50 where the owner, resident or tenant of the space must take reasonable steps to encourage physical distancing among guests. For restricted areas, only 10 people are allowed where the visitors can be of different households if receiving at a residence.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20211005030019/https://www.health.qld.gov.au/system-governance/legislation/cho-public-health-directions-under-expanded-public-health-act-powers/revoked/movement-gathering-direction-6
column51: As of 30 November 2020, although public transport has remained open for general use, there are various restrictions implemented to prevent the spread of COVID-19. Individuals are strongly suggested to physically distance, practice good hygiene and travel outside peak hours while riding public transport.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20210509110330/https://translink.com.au/sites/default/files/assets/resources/travel-information/covid-safe-transport-plan.pdf
column60: During this time period, per the Movement and Gathering Direction (No.7), as of 30 November 2020, individuals continue to not be required to stay at home unless displaying symptoms or a close contact.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20211013064817/https://www.health.qld.gov.au/system-governance/legislation/cho-public-health-directions-under-expanded-public-health-act-powers/revoked/movement-gathering-direction-7
column69: During this time period, by the "Border Restrictions Direction (No.18)", there were heavy restrictions imposed upon internal movement by the Queensland government. Any individual who has been in a COVID-19 hotspot in the past 14 days are not allowed to enter Queensland unless:  -they are a Queensland resident  -required to comply order to attend Court or Tribunal  -required to fulfil shared custody obligation  -required to assist with or participate in State, Territory or Commonwealth law enforcement investigation  -arrives to Queensland in air and directly transfers without leaving airport or remains in quarantine until time to leave  -entering higher education institution or boarding school  -entering to receive essential health care    If a person meets those exceptions, they must present a Queensland Border Declaration Pass and only enter by air from an approved airport.    Apart from that, any individual who has developed symptoms consistent with COVID-19 must undergo a COVID-19 test upon arrival.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20211014040741/https://www.health.qld.gov.au/system-governance/legislation/cho-public-health-directions-under-expanded-public-health-act-powers/revoked/border-restrictions-18
column77: As of 30 November 2020, the Queensland government has implemented programs to assist Queenslanders facing financial difficulty due to COVID-19. Apart from the federal government's JobKeeper payment being extended until 28 March 2021, the state government has been offering one-off $1500 hardship payments for Queenslanders who have faced financial difficulties during the quarantine and have contracted COVID-19 outside the workplace. There are also various job opportunity sites and mental health support websites linked by the government.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201130133223/https://www.qld.gov.au/jobs/support-workers-coronavirus
column79: As of 30 November 2020, the Queensland government has been offering debt relief for individuals. The government handed out an automatic $200 rebate to all households to assist with electricity and water bills in 2020.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201130133223/https://www.qld.gov.au/jobs/support-workers-coronavirus
column86: As of 30 November, the Queensland government has a coordinated public campaign consisting of a regularly updated website with the latest COVID-19 policies and case numbers along with social media pages and contact information.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201130183451/https://www.qld.gov.au/health/conditions/health-alerts/coronavirus-covid-19
column88: During this time period, by the most current "COVID-19 Public Health Alert No.19", all individuals showing symptoms of COVID-19 (including fever, cough, shortness of breath, loss of appetite, etc.) are strongly suggested to get tested.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201125141654/https://www.health.qld.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0020/1013258/covid-19-health-alert-19.pdf
column90: During this time period, the state government had comprehensive contact tracing for COVID-19. Any infected individuals were questioned on individuals who might have had close contact with them, who will then get contacted by staff and if not available, then an alert will be sent on both the website and social media for the dates, times and places the sick individual had gone to.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201130183326/https://www.qld.gov.au/health/conditions/health-alerts/coronavirus-covid-19/current-status/contact-tracing
column103: During this time period, although facial masks weren't required in any spaces, individuals were suggested to keep one close to them so they can wear it in the case where they cannot maintain safe social distance from others such as during large concerts and entering or exiting public transport.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201130203244/https://www.qld.gov.au/health/conditions/health-alerts/coronavirus-covid-19/protect-yourself-others/face-masks
column106: During this time period, no COVID-19 vaccines had yet been approved and been distributed for public use, hence they weren't available.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20210313004301/https://www.qld.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0024/155328/qld-vaccine-rollout.pdf
column115: During this time period, by the "Aged Care Direction (No.14)", narrow protections were implemented by the Queensland government on residential aged care facilities. Any individual cannot enter a residential aged care facility in Queensland if they have been outside Australia or a COVID-19 hotspot in the past 14 days, have symptoms consistent with COVID-19 or has not received results of COVID-19 test yet.     The operator of a residential aged care facility must develop a Workforce Management Plan which requires all employees to notify the facility of an additional place of employment and if they have become aware of a COVID-19 case being identified at additional places of employment. Contact information for all visitors must also be kept for a period of 56 days.    Visitors are only allowed to enter premises if for the purpose of an end of life visit for a resident, complies under all conditions such as reasonably practicing social distancing and wearing face masks.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20211015030743/https://www.health.qld.gov.au/system-governance/legislation/cho-public-health-directions-under-expanded-public-health-act-powers/revoked/aged-care-14

column74: As published on the Department of Home Affairs website, no foreign arrivals are permitted into the country unless they are in an exempt category or have been granted an individual exemption which includes compassionate and national interest grounds. All international arrivals must quarantine for 14 days at a designated facility. There is the possibility to travel to Australia quarantine free without an exemption if you have been in New Zealand for 14 days or more and not been in a designated COVID-19 outbreak location, and you are travelling to Australia on a quarantine-free flight from 16/10/2020.    https://web.archive.org/web/20201130233418/https://covid19.homeaffairs.gov.au/travel-restrictions    https://web.archive.org/web/20201130222312/https://covid19.homeaffairs.gov.au/new-zealand-safe-travel-zone

column15: On the Queensland Education Department Page on the 30 November, they published a outline for education in Queensland which outlined that schools are in "normal attendance mode", with no restrictions on attendance. This policy applied to all of Queensland. Schools in Queensland were not for much of this time period owing to the summer holidays.    This was a continuation of the previous policy, which saw schools open with normal attendance. However, there were requirements of maintaining physical distancing, practising good hygiene and staying home when sick at schools. This suggests a 1G restriction.    https://web.archive.org/web/20201130014209/https://qed.qld.gov.au/about-us/news-and-media/novel-coronavirus/covid-19-operating-guidelines-for-queensland-state-schools
column24: As published on the Queensland Health Website, Restrictions on Businesses, Activities and Undertakings Direction (No. 10) allowed for workplaces to reopen, but with a number of conditions. Where an employee earns more than $1,500 per fortnight, employers can use the payment to subsidise the employee’s wages.    Self-employed individuals will also be eligible to receive the JobKeeper payment. Self-employed individuals are not informal workers as they operate their own business with an ABN in order to be eligible to the JobKeeper Payment. Therefore, this scheme was available to formal workers.    This represents a 2F level of policy as of 27 April 2020 in Australia. column79: The Government of South Australia’s website (updated on 24 April 2020; archived on 16 May 2020) suggests that State Parliament had endorsed a number of initiatives aimed at helping landlords and tenants whose incomes had been affected by COVID-19 in the context of residential tenancies in South Australia.     The emergency measures acknowledged the inability for tenants to be able to fulfil their financial responsibilities to landlords as a result of circumstances beyond their control.    Measures to protect tenants include:  -	Ensured tenants cannot be evicted by landlords due to an inability to pay rent because of COVID-19 employment loss  -	Prevented landlords from increasing rent during the COVID-19 period  -	Allowed routine inspections by landlords and property managers to be conducted using technology to avoid the spread of COVID-19  -	Ensured that COVID-19 was a designated form of undue hardship for matters being heard by the South Australian Civil and Administrative Tribunal (SACAT) where disputes arise.    However, the legislation did not specify what, if any, rent reduction should occur. The government encouraged tenants to carefully consider their need to use the above measures. If a tenant had been affected by COVID-19 but could still pay their rent, they were encouraged to continue doing so.    Since these measures appear to be applied in the context of residential tenancies, it is a narrow relief.    This represents a 1 level of policy which is a continuance of the policy of significant change to pre-covid times as of 15 May 2020 in South Australia. column79: The Government of South Australia’s website (updated on 24 April 2020; archived on 16 May 2020) suggests that State Parliament had endorsed a number of initiatives aimed at helping landlords and tenants whose incomes had been affected by COVID-19 in the context of residential tenancies in South Australia.     The emergency measures acknowledged the inability for tenants to be able to fulfil their financial responsibilities to landlords as a result of circumstances beyond their control.    Measures to protect tenants include:  -	Ensured tenants cannot be evicted by landlords due to an inability to pay rent because of COVID-19 employment loss  -	Prevented landlords from increasing rent during the COVID-19 period  -	Allowed routine inspections by landlords and property managers to be conducted using technology to avoid the spread of COVID-19  -	Ensured that COVID-19 was a designated form of undue hardship for matters being heard by the South Australian Civil and Administrative Tribunal (SACAT) where disputes arise.    However, the legislation did not specify what, if any, rent reduction should occur. The government encouraged tenants to carefully consider their need to use the above measures. If a tenant had been affected by COVID-19 but could still pay their rent, they were encouraged to continue doing so.    Since these measures appear to be applied in the context of residential tenancies, it is a narrow relief.    This represents a 1 level of policy which is a continuance of the policy of significant change to pre-covid times as of 15 May 2020 in South Australia. column115: As published on WA government website, Restrictions are in place regarding visits to residential aged care facilities.  Do not visit aged care facilities if you:  have arrived in South Australia in the last 14 days  have a fever or symptoms of a respiratory infection such as a cough, sore throat or shortness of breath  have been in contact with:  a confirmed case of COVID-19 in the last 14 days  anyone with a high temperature, fever, chills, symptoms of acute respiratory infection, or loss of taste and smell, in the last 72 hours.  From 1 May 2020, you must have had your influenza vaccination to visit an aged care facility.  Aged care facilities must take extra precautions when it comes to visits. These include:  making sure visits are kept short  allowing no more than two visitors, including doctors, at a time  observing social distancing requirements  making sure visits occur in a resident’s room, outdoors, or in a specific area they designate - there should be no visiting in communal areas  ensuring there are no large group visits or gatherings, including social activities or entertainment  No school groups of any size are allowed to visit residential aged care facilities.  No children aged under 16 years are permitted to visit residential aged care facilities except in special circumstances.  If you cannot visit your family and friends in a residential aged care facility, it’s important to keep in touch. Make phone or video calls, send postcards, photos or artwork or film short videos to share.  This represents a continuation of the policy response to COVID-19.    https://web.archive.org/web/20200602164319/https://www.covid-19.sa.gov.au/restrictions-and-responsibilities/visits-to-residential-care-facilities

column74: this is a continuation of the existing policy that has been in effect since 20 March 2020. The National government is closing its border to all non-citizens and non-residents. column77: On 22 March (this is a continuation of the existing policy), the National government introduces economic support packages in response to the covid-19 pandemic which includes support for workers and households. column79: As published on Government of South Australia website, State Parliament has endorsed a number of initiatives aimed at helping landlords and tenants whose incomes have been affected by COVID-19. column77: 1. The Government’s JobKeeper Payment helped keep more Australians in jobs and support businesses affected by the significant economic impact of the coronavirus. Under the JobKeeper Payment, workers would receive a fortnightly payment of $1,500 (before tax) through their employer. The JobKeeper Payment was open to eligible businesses, not-for-profits and the self-employed who can enrol at ato.gov.au. The Payment is available from 30 March 2020 until 27 September 2020 with employers receiving the first payments from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) from the first week of May.   2. The Government was temporarily expanding eligibility to income support payments and establishing a new, time-limited Coronavirus supplement to be paid at a rate of $550 per fortnight.  This would be paid to both existing and new recipients of the JobSeeker Payment, Youth Allowance jobseeker, Parenting Payment, Farm Household Allowance and Special Benefit. The Coronavirus supplement will be paid for the next 6 months. Eligible income support recipients will receive the full amount of the $550 Coronavirus supplement on top of their payment each fortnight.  As a continuation of current policies, this was labelled as 2F. column69: On 16 June, the SA government announced an easing of some border restrictions which affects people entering from WA, Tasmania, and the NT. Travellers from all other States (i.e., Victoria and NSW) will still be subject to quarantine measures. column69: As of 22nd July 2020, there are no restrictions of internal movements within South Australia. The previous restriction on movements into abroginal communities are no longer in effect as of 10th July 2020, with the final three communities (the Anangu Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara (APY) Lands, Gerard (Riverland), and Yalata (Far West Coast))deemed Designated Areas formally exiting the Determination. column79: As published on Government of South Australia website, State Parliament has endorsed a number of initiatives aimed at helping landlords and tenants whose incomes have been affected by COVID-19. Measures to protect tenants include:  Ensuring tenants cannot be evicted by landlords due to an inability to paid rent because of COVID-19 employment loss  Preventing landlords from increasing rent during the COVID-19 period  Allowing routine inspections by landlords and property managers to be conducted using technology to avoid the spread of COVID-19  Ensuring that COVID-19 is a designated form of undue hardship for matters being heard by the South Australian Civil and Administrative Tribunal (SACAT) where disputes arise. column33: While ultimately state and territory governments have control over restrictions on public events, the federal government made some recommendations via guidelines for what these restrictions should look like. And seat allocation was advised to keep 1.5m between patrons. column33: As of 29 July 2020, public events were allowed across South Australia. This was a continuation of policies* implemented on 29 June 2020, when the SA Government entered Step 3 of its  "Roadmap to Recovery".    Public events involving 'defined public activities' (e.g. the onsite consumption of food, sporting and entertainment activities, ceremonies, auctions, and driving lessons**) were subjected to a density restriction of 1 person per 2 square metres. Attendees were also expected to maintain a physical distance of 1.5m where possible.  Reusable smoking equipment (such as hookahs) and shared utensils were prohibited. The collection of contact tracing information was mandatory at some defined public activities. column15: Schedule 1(m) of the Emergency Management (Public Activities No 6) (COVID-19) Direction 2020 (effective from 5 Aug 2020 to 13 Aug 2020) suggests that a gathering at a school, university or other educational institution or a childcare facility, or in a vehicle used for the purposes of any such institution or facility, that is necessary for the normal business of the institution or facility was not excluded from prohibited gatherings and prescribed gatherings definitions as of 5 Aug 2020.    Additionally, the Government of South Australia’s website (archived on 6 Aug 2020) suggests that all public school students are expected to attend their school or preschool. Individual schools will only be temporarily closed if there is a confirmed case of COVID-19.  Higher education facilities remain open and specific requirements are in place for people who have returned from a country or region that is at high or moderate risk for COVID-19. SA Health had advised that it was safe for students and staff to attend university, TAFE and other VET institutions and encouraged them to feel comfortable returning to attend in person when possible. However, if a person has a chronic medical condition or a compromised immune system, they should consult their GP in the first instance. If they are feeling unwell, they should stay home.    The website also refers to “Information for universities, higher education and vocational education facilities, their students and staff, " a document published by the Department of Health (Commonwealth). It suggests that people should:  -	wash their hands frequently with soap and water, before and after eating, and after going to the toilet  -	cover their cough and sneeze, dispose of tissues, and use alcohol-based hand sanitiser  -	and if unwell, avoid contact with others (stay more than 1.5 metres from people).    In addition, the Government of South Australia’s website (archived on 5 Aug 2020) also suggests that people practise good hygiene and keep 1.5 metres distance from others wherever, whenever possible.    This represents a 1G level of policy which is a continuance of the policy of significant change to pre-covid times as of 5 Aug 2020 in South Australia. column24: According to the SA Government website as of 6 August 2020, food and beverages could only be consumed by customers who were seated at tables, and not at bars or in ordering areas. This was a minor tightening of existing restrictions which did not trigger a change in the ordinal scale.    Other workplace restrictions remained the same:    In general, businesses were prohibited from providing shared utensils when serving food or reusable smoking and vaping equipment. Communal food and beverage service areas (such as communal buffets, salad bars, and beverage dispensers) were also prohibited.    Workplaces which conducted defined public activities (such as the onsite consumption of food and drink, sport and recreation activities, indoor public meetings, ceremonies, the provision of personal care services, the operation of nightclubs and licensed premises, property auctions and inspections, and driving classes) were required to follow the 1 person per 2 square metre density rule. Patrons and employees at these workplaces were to take reasonable steps to maintain physical distancing. Some venues hosting defined public activities were required to collect visitor contact details for contact tracing purposes. All workplaces hosting defined public activities were required to have a COVID-Safe plan which outlined how staff and visitors would be kept safe from COVID-19. Workplaces hosting prescribed activities with over 1,000 people attending were required to have an approved COVID Management Plan.    Some workplaces (including retail and grocery stores as well as workplaces providing some essential services) were exempt from the rules imposed on defined public activities. column79: The Government of South Australia’s website (updated on 22 Jul 2020; archived on 6 Aug 2020) suggests that State Parliament had endorsed a number of initiatives aimed at helping landlords and tenants whose incomes had been affected by COVID-19 in relation to residential tenancies in South Australia.     The emergency measures acknowledged tenants' inability to fulfil their financial responsibilities to landlords as a result of circumstances beyond their control.     Measures to protect tenants include:   - Ensuring tenants cannot be evicted by landlords due to an inability to pay rent because of COVID-19 employment loss   - Preventing landlords from increasing rent during the COVID-19 period   - Ensured that COVID-19 was a designated form of undue hardship for matters being heard by the South Australian Civil and Administrative Tribunal (SACAT) where disputes arise.     However, the legislation does not specify what, if any, rent reduction should occur. The government encourages tenants to carefully consider their need to use the above measures. If a tenant has been affected by COVID-19 but can still pay their rent, they are encouraged to continue doing so. Since these measures appear to be applied in the context of residential tenancies, it is a narrow relief.     This represents a 1 level of policy which is a continuation of existing COVID-19 support measures in South Australia. column24: There is no state variation in COVID-19 policy.    According to the SA Government website as of 21 August 2020, COVID marshals are required in some businesses from 21 August. These marshals are responsible for ensuring COVID-safe measures are in place. The following activities are required to have a COVID marshal:     -The onsite purchase and consumption of food or beverages (indoor and outdoor). This does not include take-away only operators.   -Religious or faith-based ceremonies.   -Supermarkets and hardware stores.   -Distribution centres (including associated transport operations).   -Gymnasiums and fitness centres.   -Swimming pools used by the public.   -Social and sporting clubs.   -Any activity where a COVID Management Plan is required (i.e. large activities with over 1,000 attendees).  - Any operation which may be defined by the state coordinator.     This represents a tightening of the policy and is in place across SA.     Other workplace restrictions remain the same:     All businesses that conduct a defined public activity must have a COVID-Safety plan. Defined public activities include:     -the onsite purchase and consumption of food or beverages (whether occurring in an indoor or outdoor area)   -sport (including sports training), fitness or recreation activities   -indoor public meetings   -ceremonies   -the provision of personal care services   -the provision of public entertainment   -the provision of recreational transport  -the operation of a nightclub   -the operation of relevant licensed premises   -the operation of a casino or gaming area   -auctions and inspections of premises for the purpose of sale or rental of any property  -driver instruction.     Defined public activities needed to follow occupancy requirements of 1 person per 2 square metres. Specific businesses (such as gaming machine venues, indoor fitness classes, indoor public meetings, personal care services, ceremonies, weddings, funeral services, auctions and inspections, provision of recreational transport, digital instruction) require contact tracing information to be collected.     Other general restrictions are in place:   - utensils cannot be shared   - communal food or beverage services are prohibited  - Re-usable smoking equipment (such as hookahs) are prohibited    https://web.archive.org/web/20200821230754/https://www.covid-19.sa.gov.au/restrictions-and-responsibilities/activities-and-gatherings
column33: From 21 August 2020, events, businesses, and activities were required to have a COVID Marshal (who is in charge of ensuring that COVID-19 rules are in place) if they involved any of the following:   - The onsite purchase and consumption of food or beverages (indoor and outdoor). column74: According to a joint media released published by the Australian Minister for Health and the Chief Medical Officer published on 2 March 2020, healthcare and residential aged care workers arriving in Australia from Italy and South Korea were asked not to attend work for 14 days after arriving in Australia. This was an escalation of public health advice directed towards individuals arriving from Italy and South Korea.    Existing travel restrictions imposed on individuals arriving from China and Iran remained the same:  Foreign nationals who had been in Iran or China within the past 14 days were prohibited from entering Australia. Australian citizens, permanent residents and immediate family members who had been in Iran or China in the past 14 days were required to quarantine at home for 14 days after arriving in Australia.     Archived links:  https://web.archive.org/web/20220121004113/https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22media%2Fpressrel%2F7216775%22  https://web.archive.org/web/20220121011945/https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22media%2Fpressrel%2F7218407%22

According to a joint media release from the Australian Prime Minister, the Minister for Health, and the Minister for Foreign Affairs and Minister for Women, foreign nationals who had been in the Republic of Korea on or after 5 March 2020 were prohibited from entering Australia for 14 days from the time they had left or transited through Korea. Australian citizens, permanent residents and immediate family members who had been in Iran in the past 14 days were required to quarantine at home for 14 days after arriving in Australia.   Enhanced health screening and temperature checking arrangements were implemented for individuals arriving in Australia from Italy during this time.    This was a tightening of measures imposed on individuals arriving from the Republic of Korea and Italy. column77: According to the Treasury, the JobKeeper Payment became available introduced from 30 March 2020 until 27 September 2020.    The JobKeeper Payment is a payment made to eligible businesses and not-for-profits affected by the Coronavirus to support them in retaining employees. Businesses must have paid their employees before they are entitled to receive the JobKeeper payment.     Where an employee’s total remuneration is less than $1,500 per fortnight (before tax), or has been stood down, the employer must provide the employee at least $1,500 per fortnight (before tax). Where an employee earns more than $1,500 per fortnight, employers can use the payment to subsidise the employee’s wages.    Self-employed individuals will also be eligible to receive the JobKeeper payment. Self-employed individuals are not informal workers as they operate their own business with an ABN in order to be eligible to the JobKeeper Payment. Therefore, this scheme was available to formal workers.    This represents a 2F level of policy as of 27 April 2020 in Australia.    Archived link:  https://web.archive.org/web/20220304125206/https://treasury.gov.au/sites/default/files/2020-04/JobKeeper_frequently_asked_questions_2.pdf

See: https://web.archive.org/web/20220517043637/https://www.pm.gov.au/media/supporting-australian-workers-and-business     Additionally, on 30 March 2020, the National government announces providing job keeper payment for formal workers with flat payment of $1,500 per fortnight through their employers for up to six months (until September). As stated on the Prime Minister official website, this payment will provide the equivalent of around 70 per cent of the national median wage, hence coded as 2 (> 50% median salary). See: https://web.archive.org/web/20220511073206/https://www.pm.gov.au/media/130-billion-jobkeeper-payment-keep-australians-job
column88: This is a continuation of the existing policy.  As published on the DoH website (last updated on 2 April), the national government provides general guidelines for who can be tested that is those that develop fever or respiratory symptoms and meet at least one of the following criteria:  •	you have returned from overseas in the past 14 days  •	you have been in close contact with someone diagnosed with COVID-19 in the past 14 days  •	you travelled on a cruise ship (either passenger or crew) in the 14 days before developing symptoms  •	you are a health care, aged care or residential care worker  •	you have lived in an area where there is a higher risk of community transmission, as defined by the local public health unit  Or they should also be tested if meeting all the following criteria:   •	you are in hospital  •	you have fever and serious respiratory symptoms  •	there is no other clear cause of the symptoms  People in high-risk settings (e.g., aged & residential care facilities) will be tested if there are 2 or more people with fever and respiratory symptoms in the setting.  Some states and territories may have more testing criteria based on their cases.    https://web.archive.org/web/20200402205514/https://www.health.gov.au/news/health-alerts/novel-coronavirus-2019-ncov-health-alert/what-you-need-to-know-about-coronavirus-covid-19    However, on 24 April, National Cabinet agreed to expand testing criteria across Australia to all people with mild symptoms of COVID-19. This will ensure cases are quickly identified.     https://web.archive.org/web/20220515093016/https://www.pm.gov.au/media/update-coronavirus-measures-24april20

column15: In term 2 (approximately from late April 2020 to early July 2020), students will continue to learn at home where possible, with teachers leading this learning. All schools (Government and Non-Government) remain open for those students who are unable to be supported/supervised at home. column24: Office workers are encouraged to work from home when possible.   TAS government has released a series of lists of businesses that are not allowed to open since March (the continuation of the existing policy). The list includes a specific non-essential businesses such as:   •	Restaurants and cafés will be restricted to takeaway and/or home delivery  •	Hairdressers and barber shops - limited to 1 person per 4 square metre rule and personal contact minimised as much as possible  •	Gyms and indoor sporting venues  •	Community facilities, such as halls, clubs and RSLs  •	Beauty therapy, tanning, waxing, manicure or other nail treatments, tattoos, ear and body piercing, body modification and other similar services  •	Pubs, registered and licensed clubs and hotels, other than the part of those premises that are legally allowed to sell takeaway alcohol (eg. bottle shops)  https://web.archive.org/web/20200407131150/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/business-and-employees/business-restrictions  https://web.archive.org/web/20200419191319/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/important-information-for-people-in-north-west-tasmania
column33: All public events are banned following the stay-at-home requirements since Tuesday 14 April 2020.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200506143404/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/gatherings/gatherings-faqs
column42: This is a continuation of the existing policy announced by the Tasmania Premier on 30 March (then officially extended on 17 April for a further four weeks).   The maximum number of people at a public gathering is two people, except for gatherings of household members, those in shared parenting arrangements, guardianship arrangements or other care arrangements”.  Other exceptions apply for:   -	Wedding with the total number of people present does not exceed 5 persons and is subject to 4 square meters rules.   -	Funeral with total number of people present does not exceed 10 persons and is subject to 4 square meters rules.     TAS gov issues an additional measure in response to covid-19 cluster in North-West area in mid-April, however, it doesn’t affect the existing gathering restriction in place, thus, coded ‘general’ (no regional variation) - see: https://web.archive.org/web/20200419195514/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0029/88067/Gatherings-North-West-Region-No.-2-17-Apr-20.pdf  https://web.archive.org/web/20220326020739/https://www.premier.tas.gov.au/releases/restrictions_in_place_for_a_further_four_weeks  https://web.archive.org/web/20220429024321/https://www.gazette.tas.gov.au/editions/2020/march_2020/21959_-_Special_31_March_2020.pdf
column51: Metro Tasmania are reducing cash transactions on board. Greencards are free from 26 March, and travel will be free from Thursday 26 March until Sunday 31 May 2020 (extended from Friday 10 April) to give people time to get a free Greencard. To minimise person-to-person contact, all bus services across the state are currently provided free of charge to eliminate cash handling on board. A fare amnesty has been put in place until 31 May 2020 to allow all passengers time to adjust to a cashless public bus system. There are strict capacity limits in place for public transports.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200507014623/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/public-transport
column60: Based on the Tasmanian gov gazette published on 7 April on stay-at-home directions (set to be in effect starting 8 April to 27 April), Tasmania must not leave their home unless for essential purpose such as:   -	shop for essential food and supplies or services.  -	receive medical care  -	for compassionate needs or social support (including facilitating shared custody, guardianship or care arrangements for another person)  -	exercise  -	attend work, volunteering, school and study, where it cannot be done remotely  -	take a pet to a veterinarian  -	perform essential maintenance on another premises owned by them  This direction appears to be the official enforcement of the stay-at-home policy announced in late March.     TAS gov issues an additional measure in response to covid-19 cluster in North-West area in mid-April, however, it doesn’t affect the existing stay-at-home policy that’s already in place, thus, codes 'general' (no regional variation).     https://web.archive.org/web/20200419195514/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0029/88067/Gatherings-North-West-Region-No.-2-17-Apr-20.pdf  https://web.archive.org/web/20200407045818/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/gatherings/gatherings-faqs  https://web.archive.org/web/20220425094202/https://www.gazette.tas.gov.au/editions/2020/april_2020/21969_-_Special_8_April_2020.pdf.pdf  https://web.archive.org/web/20220429023242/https://www.premier.tas.gov.au/covid-19_updates/press_conference_-_30_march_2020

column15: According to the Tasmanian Government’s website (updated on 20 May 2020), students will come back to school-based learning through a phased approach in Term 2. Different schools had different approaches. For instance, students in the North West of Tasmania were able to return to school to commence Term 2 on Monday, 4 May. Kindergarten to Year 6 students will return to learning at school from 25 May 2020 as per the Tasmanian Department of Education.    All schools are working hard to apply Public Health and Australian Health Protection Principal Committee (AHPPC) guidance to their site’s practices. Schools are also applying guidance from WorkSafe Tasmania’s COVID-19 Safe Workplaces Framework. The most important strategies for schools and the Education and Care sector to implement to assist families in staying healthy include:  -	Promoting personal hygiene and cough and sneeze etiquette  -	Additional cleaning (especially of frequently touched surfaces)  -	Encouraging physical distancing by cancelling or postponing a range of activities  -	Supporting staff and families to stay home if they are unwell  -	Supporting those who are more at risk of severe illness if they contract COVID-19  -	Looking after the psychological wellbeing of students, staff and families.    This represents a level 2G policy as of 21 May 2020 in Tasmania. column51: On 20 March 2020, the TAS Minister for Infrastructure and Transport announced public transport would be continuing as it was not affected by the advice against holding large gatherings. This was reiterated on 24 March by the Tasmanian Department of State Growth.    Additionally, the Tasmanian Department of Health suggests that people can attend school or work, obtain supplies or attend medical appointments. If people are using public transport for any of the reasons permitted under the Direction to stay at home, that is fine.    Additionally, the Tasmanian Government suggests the following measures:  -	Passengers are encouraged to keep physically distancing in mind and choose a seat away from others where possible.  -	Anyone feeling unwell should avoid using public transport.  -	For short trips, consider walking or cycling.  -	Travel outside peak periods where possible.  -	Adults seeking to board a bus which has a high number of passengers are asked to consider waiting for the next service where available. This request does not apply to children.  -	Practice good hand hygiene. If possible, use hand sanitiser before and after catching the bus.  -	Spread out on board as much as you can. Members of the same household and family groups can sit together.  -	Avoid touching surfaces inside the bus whenever you can.    This represents a 1G level of policy as of 21 May 2020 in Tasmania. column74: International Travel Restrictions    The National Cabinet noted the AHPPC’s advice on high-risk countries for COVID-19 importation risk and its continued support for the 14 day self isolation requirement for all returning travellers.  The National Cabinet welcomed the Commonwealth Government’s decision to stop the entry of non-citizens and non-permanent residents and their immediate families into Australia after 9pm AEDT on Friday 20 March 2020 in order to align international travel restrictions with the risks. Limited exemptions will be available under the authority of the Australian Border Force Commissioner, focused on individuals providing critical or essential services or on compassionate grounds. This represents a continuation of the policy response to COVID-19.    https://web.archive.org/web/20200617021520/https://treasury.gov.au/coronavirus/jobkeeper  https://web.archive.org/web/20220517043637/https://www.pm.gov.au/media/supporting-australian-workers-and-business

column24: All businesses and workplaces are now permitted to operate since 26 June. However, all businesses operating are required to implement measures to meet the minimum COVID-19 safety standards and record this in a COVID-19 Safety plan. Where practicable, business operators, staff, volunteers and attendees should maintain a distance of 1.5 metres from other people.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200625165705/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/business-and-employees/business-restrictions  https://web.archive.org/web/20200701131637/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/business-and-employees/business-restrictions
column33: Tasmania Government eases the business restrictions from 26 Jane and Public events are allowed with a cap on the number of participants. The number of people permitted at businesses/activities (other than households) is now determined by the density of the area, up to a maximum of 250 people for an undivided space in an indoor premises; and 500 people in an undivided space outdoors. The maximum density limit is one person per 2 square metres.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200701131637/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/business-and-employees/business-restrictions

column15: Since Tuesday 9 June, all school students who are well are expected to be learning back in the classroom. Nonetheless, students with health concerns that make them more vulnerable to COVID-19 will be supported to continue learning at home where possible. Furthermore, the Tasmanian Government has introduced precautionary measures to limit the impact of COVID-19 in schools such as social distancing measures.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200701131632/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/schools-and-childcare
column51: Gathering limits do not apply to public transport. Still, passengers are encouraged to keep physical distancing in mind and choose a seat away from others where possible. Cashless payments are preferred. Metro Tasmania has implemented an enhanced cleaning regime of its bus fleet by its contractor, with particular attention being paid to frequently touched surfaces.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200701131619/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/transport
column60: There are no stay at home requirements in place in Tasmania. Recreational activities and internal travel within Tasmania are permitted.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200701131605/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/current-restrictions
column79: The Tasmanian Government is offering broad debt and contract relief. This can be seen through the government's Business Vehicle Registration Relief Package, funding for registered arts organisations, and licence fees waivers for certain commercial fishers and processors. Also, there are changes to residential tenancies including suspension of evictions, immediate halt to any increases in rent, and ability to reduce rent by mutual agreement.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200703115932/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/stimulus-and-support/businesses-and-industries  https://web.archive.org/web/20200701131609/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/business-and-employees/business-support
column86: The Tasmanian Government has a dedicated website for the pandemic. The website is connected to the government's social media profiles.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200701131607/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/facts/resources  https://web.archive.org/web/20200702010429/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/facts/where-to-find-information
column88: Anyone exhibiting symptoms of COVID-19, no matter how mild, is eligible for a test.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200701131705/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/keeping-yourself-safe/testing-for-covid19
column90: The Tasmanian Government publishes statistics on the pandemic on its COVID response website. The Tasmanian Department of Health posts regular updates on cases on its social media page.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200618123053/https://www.facebook.com/HealthTas/posts  https://web.archive.org/web/20200701131528/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/facts/cases-and-testing-updates
column103: Masks are recommended to individuals who are suspected or known to have the virus and people in close contact (within 1.5 metres) of someone suspected or known to be infected. This is normally only healthcare workers and carers. Healthy individual do not have to wear face-masks. People who are sick with COVID-19 should wear a face-mask (if they can) when they need to leave quarantine, for example when they get tested or go to see a doctor.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200618124148/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/keeping-yourself-safe/what-you-can-do/facemasks
column115: Each resident may have one visit a day, by up to two visitors, for no longer than two hours. All visitors must have an influenza vaccination. Visitors are barred from entry if they have been in contact with COVID patients, travelled interstate or overseas in the last 14 days, or display symptoms of COVID. Operators of aged care facilities must screen all people before they enter the premises to see if they comply with current restrictions.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200618124441/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/aged-care-facility-visits

column74: The Australian borders are closed. Only Australian citizens, residents, and immediate family members can travel to Australia.  Travellers arriving from any country may undergo enhanced health screening on arrival in Australia. All arrivals will be quarantined for 14 days and state and territory travel restrictions may also apply.      https://web.archive.org/web/20200630225042/https://www.health.gov.au/news/health-alerts/novel-coronavirus-2019-ncov-health-alert/coronavirus-covid-19-advice-for-travellers

column15: "As at 6 July  2020, there are measures in place relating to education . Namely, these measures relate to :  - Promoting personal hygiene and cough and sneeze etiquette  - Additional cleaning (especially of frequently touched surfaces)  - Encouraging physical distancing by cancelling or postponing a range of activities and reducing intermixing of years  - Supporting staff and families to stay home if they are unwell  - Supporting those who are more at risk of severe illness if they contract COVID-19  -Looking after the psychological wellbeing of students, staff and families.  Furthermore, school gatherings are also generally cancelled. In particular, the gatherings are:  - assemblies and presentation nights  - excursions  - travel  - fetes and fairs  - concerts (with audiences)  - sports carnivals  - school camps (both local and interstate)  - face-to-face parent teacher meetings.  However, school-related activities and events will be reintroduced, e.g. carnivals and parent-teacher interviews, from Term 3 (20 July).   This is a continuation of the policy and is in place across Tasmania.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200710144111/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/schools-and-childcare"
column24: "As at 6 July 2020, there are some measures in place relating to workspace. All workplaces should develop a COVID Safe Workplace Plan.  All businesses are open. Patrons must be seated in premises where alcohol is sold.   Social distancing of 1.5m is also expected.  The maximum number of people permitted on premises includes staff, volunteers, children and babies.   This represents a continuance of the policy and is in place across Tasmania. There does not appear to be any variation due to vaccination status.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200704133521/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/business-and-employees/business-restrictions  "
column33: "As at 6 July 2020, there are requirements in place for events. These apply across Tasmania.   There are physical density requirements allowing 1 per 2 square metres per person. There are maximum density limits of 250 people for an undivided space in an indoor premises and 500 people in an undivided space outdoors.   This policy represents a continuance of the policy.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200704133521/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/business-and-employees/business-restrictions"
column51: "As at 6 July 2020, there are no measures in place relating to public transport. This is in place across Tasmania. column60: "As at 6 July 2020, there are no measures in place relating to stay at home. This relates to all of Tasmania - there is no state differentiation. It is also encouraged that the following people are tested:  - All persons presenting with respiratory symptoms, or with history of recent respiratory symptoms (within the last 7 days)  - Healthcare workers displaying symptoms or healthcare workers without symptoms. column90: "As of 6 July 2020, the Tasmanian Government is recording statistics relating to the number of COVID cases.This includes also where the current cases are located. This is updated regularly.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200705000902/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/"
column103: "As at 6 July 2020, face masks are not required. Face masks are recommended if a person is unwell with COVID-19 symptoms and need to be around other people.   This is a continuance of the policy. This is in place across Tasmania.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200703184618/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/keeping-yourself-safe/what-you-can-do"
column106: "As at 6 July 2020, the vaccine is not available to anyone   This represents a continuation of the policy and is in place across Tasmania.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200703184618/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/keeping-yourself-safe/what-you-can-do"
column115: "As at 6 July 2020, there are restrictions on visits to high risk settings.  Aged care facilities have the following restrictions:  - each resident is allowed one visit a day up to two visitors  - visits will occur in the resident's room  - all visitors must have a flu vaccine  - additional visitors are allowed for end of life support or to provide essential support requested by faciity  - visitors must not have been overseas or interstate in the past 14 days, have any COVID symptoms, been in contact with anyone with COVID-19  This policy is in place across Tasmania. It represents a continuance of the policy.   https://web.archive.org/web/20200705091351/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/aged-care-facility-visits"

column74: As of 8 July 2020, Australia’s borders are closed. Only Australian citizens, residents and immediate family members can travel to Australia. Travellers arriving from any country may undergo enhanced health screening on arrival in Australia. All arrivals will be quarantined for 14 days and state and territory travel restrictions may also apply.  Since 25 March 2020, all Australian citizens and permanent residents have been prohibited from travelling out of Australia unless granted an exemption.  https://web.archive.org/web/20200630225042/https://www.health.gov.au/news/health-alerts/novel-coronavirus-2019-ncov-health-alert/coronavirus-covid-19-advice-for-travellers  https://web.archive.org/web/20200723112929/https://www.health.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2020/05/coronavirus-covid-19-information-for-international-travellers.pdf

column15: During this time period, Tasmanian schools of all levels continue to operate face to face with the oncoming arrival of Term 3. Schools are advised to operate with various preventative measures taken to protect against COVID-19 such as promoting personal hygiene, encouraging physical distancing  and supporting staff and families to stay home if unwell. School events such as assemblies and sport carnivals are also slowly being reintroduced with appropriate protective measures. In cases of a confirmed COVID-19 case appearing at a school, temporary site closure is most likely to occur.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200715091000/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/schools-and-childcare
column24: During this time period, all businesses and workplaces are allowed to normally operate although with various restrictions. All businesses are expected to take appropriate measures against COVID-19 and record them in a Safety Plan. There is also a maximum density limit of 1 person per 2 square metres imposed on business grounds where all individuals are included except for particular premises such as airports, medical facilities, courts, educational facilities and emergency services.     Also, when alcohol is sold, the patron must be seated and social distancing should be observed whenever possible.     Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200715090925/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/business-and-employees/business-restrictions
column33: During this time period, as long as government restrictions were abided by, public events were allowed to be held. A maximum density limit of 1 person per 2 metres was imposed along with a cap of 250 people for an undivided indoor space and 500 people for an undivided outdoor space. Patrons must be seated when alcohol is sold and social distancing should be encouraged.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200715090925/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/business-and-employees/business-restrictions
column51: During this time period, public transport was open for individuals to use although with some protective measures. Although gathering limits do not apply to public transport, passengers are still encouraged to socially distance and avoid using if unwell or if the transport has a high number of passengers already. Hygiene and using outside of peak hours are also encouraged.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200715082016/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/transport
column60: During this time period, as long as individuals abided by the various restrictions imposed by the Tasmanian government in any public gatherings, they were allowed to go outside of their homes.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200715081452/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/keeping-yourself-safe/gatherings-density-and-physical-distancing
column69: During this time period, all non-essential travellers travelling to Tasmania will be forced to enter quarantine for 14 days, provided they have evidence of residency, do not have COVID-19 and have not been overseas or on a cruise ship with 14 days of arriving. Tasmanian residents not coming back from Victoria are allowed to quarantine at their residences. Essential travellers are able to avoid the 14 day quarantine but still must report any possible COVID-19 symptoms that appear.    The large exception is for anybody who has travelled to Victoria in the past 14 days before arrival, who are not allowed into Tasmania while Tasmanian residents who come back from Victoria must quarantine in government provided accomodation.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200715080957/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/travellers-and-visitors/coming-to-tasmania
column77: During this time period, there was income support offered by the Tasmanian government. Under the Pandemic Isolation Assistance Grants, eligible individuals were able to claim a one-off payment of $250 per adult and $125 per child who were required to self isolate due to COVID-19 with a cap at $1000 per household.     To be eligible, the individual must have been required by Public Health to self-isolate as evidenced by Letter of Isolation or other official advice, be low-income or demonstrate genuine financial hardship and unable to quarantine at regular residence or with family and friends to avoid exposing vulnerable individuals to risk.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200715080945/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/stimulus-and-support/household
column79: During this period, there were debt/contract relief policies implemented by the Tasmanian government. The Private Rental Incentives Program offers landlords an incentive to set their rent to affordable prices for two-year period to individuals off the Housing Register and the COVID-19 Rent Relief Fund was established to assist tenants in financial hardship, offering up to $2000 or four weeks rent.    There is also a one-off $200 payment for guardians for every child in the care to purchase essential cleaning or hygiene products. The National Debt Helpline is also available for any suffering individuals.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200715080945/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/stimulus-and-support/household
column86: During this time period, the Tasmanian government had set up a coordinated public campaign with a regularly updated website containing latest state policies concerning COVID-19 and new case numbers as well as a public health hotline.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200721100738/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/
column88: During this time period, government covered COVID-19 tests were recommended from anyone suffering from symptoms such as a fever, runny nose, cough or sore throat as well as close contacts and people who have travelled outside Tasmania in past 14 days at various testing sites in Tasmania. Tests are offered for all ages.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200715080917/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/keeping-yourself-safe/testing-for-covid19
column90: During this time period, the Tasmanian government had comprehensive contact tracing implemented designed to counter COVID-19. Close contacts are heavily encouraged to get tested and are asked about any individuals they have been in close contact with in past 48 hours. Through the government COVIDSAFE app, individuals are notified if anyone they've been near has been confirmed as a COVID case to enhance responsive measures.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200715080933/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/keeping-yourself-safe/covidsafe-app
column103: During this time period, wearing facial masks weren't required but recommended as a preventative measure, especially if an individual displays COVID-19 symptoms and needs to be around other individuals. The Tasmanian government also suggests other measures such as social distancing and good hygiene.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200715080952/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/keeping-yourself-safe/what-you-can-do
column106: During this time period, no COVID-19 vaccines had yet been approved by the Tasmanian government for public distribution.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20220105075212/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/vaccination-information/covid-19-vaccination/where-to-get-a-vaccine
column115: During this time period, there were narrow protections implemented for residential aged care facilities (RACFs). Only two people were allowed to visit a resident at a time, although there can be multiple visits, where all visitors must have been vaccinated against influenza. Staff are also expected to have taken the influenza vaccination. However, if the resident is on end-of-life support or individual requested to provide essential support to resident to reduce distress caused by medical condition, the above limits do not apply.     Individuals under 16 and visiting services are also allowed to attend RACFS and residents can leave the facility. Operators are required to screen all individuals before allowing them on premises. Any individual who has been interstate or overseas in past 14 days, displays symptoms of COVID-19 or been in close contact with symptomatic individual are heavily suggested to not visit.     Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200715090823/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/aged-care-facility-visits

column15: For term 3, which began on 20 July, all students attended school in person, except those who were unwell or had health conditions that put them at higher risk from COVID-19. Changes from pre-COVID-19 conditions included enhanced cleaning, greater emphasis on hygiene, social distancing between adults (but not students), cancelling some activities, and closing schools with confirmed COVID-19 cases. Some assemblies, excursions, sports carnivals, inter-school competitions and parent-teacher meetings were allowed to go ahead with social distancing and hygiene measures. column115: According to the TAS Government:  In Tasmania, visits to residential aged care facilities are permitted for people providing care and support, with the following restrictions:    No more than two people can visit each resident at any time.  Visits must take place in the resident’s room, outdoors, or in a non-communal area, as designated by the facility.  Visitors must not have any symptoms of acute respiratory infection, including fever (higher than 37.5 degrees), history of fever (eg chills, night sweats), cough, sore throat, runny nose or shortness of breath.  Visitors must not have been interstate or overseas in the previous 14 days.  Visitors must not have had contact with anyone known to have COVID-19, or reasonably suspected of having COVID-19, within the previous 14 days (except as part of their employment while wearing effective personal protective equipment).  All visitors must have had the 2020 influenza vaccine (see below).  People wanting to visit an aged care facility to provide end-of-life support as a significant person to a resident can seek exemption from restrictions 4–6 above (see below).    Operators of aged care facilities must screen all people before they enter the premises.    Each resident may receive multiple visits each day, subject to each service’s policies.    The maximum duration of visits is subject to each service’s policies.    Children under the age of 16 years and visiting services such as hairdressers and allied health professionals may visit aged care facilities.    Residents may leave the facility, for example with family and friends.  Archived from: https://web.archive.org/web/20200909164313/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/aged-care-facility-visits

column24: "As at 1 October 2020, there are some measures in place relating to workspace. All workplaces should develop a COVID Safe Workplace Plan.  All businesses are open. column79: Debt and contract relief measures enacted by the Tasmanian Government were mostly limited to changes in residential tenancy rules. column86: The Tasmanian government continues to run a coordinated public campaign on COVID-19. This includes the Government's COVID-19 website (see link below) which serves as a hub for information related to COVID-19 in Tasmania, including news updates, statistics, current restrictions and COVID-19 safety advice, information for travellers, and accessing support. See https://web.archive.org/web/20201012153159/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/
column88: The Tasmanian Government advises people to get tested if they have, or have recently had, typical symptoms of COVID-19 (e.g. fever, runny nose, cough, sore throat, shortness of breath, loss of taste/smell) or hay fever symptoms (runny nose, sneezing, itchy/sore/watery eyes, or cough). Testing is also encouraged for people at high risk of exposure (e.g. health care workers, aged care workers, or their household members), close contacts of confirmed cases, and people in quarantine, but otherwise is not recommended for people without symptoms.   This is a continuation of previous policy. See https://web.archive.org/web/20201012050726/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/keeping-yourself-safe/testing-for-covid19.
column90: During this time, the Tasmanian government's COVID-19 testing web page (https://web.archive.org/web/20201019093532/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/keeping-yourself-safe/testing-for-covid19) indicates that people who test positive will be contacted by Public Health to "talk about the next steps" (presumably including contact tracing). column106: COVID-19 vaccines were not yet available during this time period. The COVID-19 vaccine rollout in Tasmania started in the last week of February 2021 (https://web.archive.org/web/20210219022536/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/vaccination-information/covid-19-vaccination)
column115: Family members and friends may visit residents of aged care facilities, with some restrictions:  -	Only two people can visit each resident at a time  -	Visits cannot take place in communal areas within the facility (e.g. may be in the resident's room, or outdoors).  -	Visitors must not have any symptoms of a respiratory infection (e.g. fever >37.5 degrees, chills, night sweats, cough, sore throat, runny nose, shortness of breath)  -	Visitors must be vaccinated against influenza  -	Visitors must not have been interstate or overseas in the last 14 days  -	Visitors must not have been in contact with a suspected or confirmed COVID-19 case in the last 14 days.   This is largely a continuation of existing policy. See https://web.archive.org/web/20201019094001/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/aged-care-facility-visits

column15: During this time period, continuing from previous policy, schools remain open for Term 4 although various restrictions were set in place to protect against COVID-19. Various strategies such as practicing good personal hygiene, additional cleaning and encouraging physical distancing was promoted by schools and any children feeling unwell with cold/flu symptoms were suggested to stay home until symptoms come to pass. If a confirmed case is found at a school, temporary site closure may occur for contact tracing and cleaning.    School events have slowly been reintroduced, subject to proper hygiene practices, gathering restrictions and physical distancing with end of year activities being allowed from 29 October 2020 where restrictions on dancing were lifted as long as they take place in separate space from food and beverages. Visitor screening was also required.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201102100203/https://coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/schools-and-childcare
column24: During this time period, continuing from previous policy, businesses remain open but are required to implement protections against COVID-19 and record them into a Safety Plan. A maximum person limit is imposed on premises, counting staff, with 250 people for undivided indoor space and 1000 people for undivided outdoor space while maximum density limit is two people per square metre. These limits are excluded for various premises however, namely health service facilities, emergency services and aged care facilities.    Additionally, although individuals can now perform standing activities, they must remain seated while consuming alcohol. Dancing must be prearranged and set in separate space from food and drinks, with the exception being a wedding.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201026200509/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/business-and-employees/business-restrictions
column33: During this time period, public events are allowed to occur but with people limits and physical distancing of at least 1.5 metres. Only 20 visitors are allowed at a household residence at one time while there is a limit of 250 people in undivided indoor spaces and 1000 people in outdoor spaces for gatherings. There is also a density limit of 2 people per square metre.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201026205444/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/gatherings-density-and-physical-distancing
column51: During this time period, although all individuals were allowed to use public transport and no gathering limits applied, they were still advised to social distance and practice good hygiene. Any unwell individuals are advised to avoid public transport as well as travelling outside peak periods if possible and using cashless ticket options.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201026204138/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/transport
column60: Continuing from previous policy, there are no government requirements for individuals to remain at home in Tasmania as long as individuals comply by restrictions on gatherings and household visits (only 20 people allowed at one time). The government also recommends physical distancing as well as practicing good hygiene.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201026203800/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/families-community/current-restrictions
column69: During this time period, restrictions on internal movement between states and territories differ by the level of risk of the area determined by the Tasmanian government.     For low-risk domestic areas, there is no need to quarantine but individuals who have spent time in these areas in past 14 days are required to register travel and contact details via TAS e-travel system a maximum of three days prior to arrival.    For medium-risk areas and high-risk domestic areas, travellers are required to quarantine and submit their intended quarantine location, preferably via the G2G system, unless they are an Essential Traveller where they can request full or partial exemption from quarantine for medium-risk areas or have done 14 days quarantine in another jurisdiction for high-risk areas.      https://web.archive.org/web/20201026195443/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/travellers-and-visitors/coming-to-tasmania
column79: During this time period, there are some forms of debt relief offered by the Tasmanian government. The Private Rental Incentives Program offers landlords an incentives to lease rent at affordable price for two years to clients off the Housing Register and the COVID-19 Rent Relief Fund offers tenants in financial hardship with support up to $2000 or four weeks' rent.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201026195738/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/stimulus-and-support/household
column86: Continuing from previous policy, the Tasmanian government continues to maintain a regularly updated website recording daily COVID-19 cases as well as any changes to state policies concerning COVID-19 for public view. column88: Continuing from previous policy, any individual who displayed symptoms of COVID-19, such as fever, runny rose, cough and sore throat, were heavily suggested to take a COVID-19 test as well as any individual with higher risk of exposure with atypical symptoms, symptomatic household members of healthcare and aged care workers, close contacts or people in quarantine. These tests can be done at a wide range of medical clinics and is government-funded.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201026195542/https://www.coronavirus.tas.gov.au/keeping-yourself-safe/testing-for-covid19
column90: Continuing from previous policy, although contact tracing was not made compulsory until 13 November 2020, there is evidence that it was being conducted during this time period. column106: During this time period, no COVID-19 vaccines had yet been approved by the Tasmanian government for public use, which would take until early February 2021. column115: During this time period, continuing from previous policy, there were various restrictions placed on visitors and staff to protect residents in aged care facilities. column88: According to Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) Case and contact management guidelines for health services and general practitioners (15 March 2020, Version 13) published by the Department of Health and Human Services (Victoria), it suggests that when a patient presents to a general practice or community health service who may be a suspected case of COVID-19, they will determine whether the patient needs testing for Covid-19.    If it is agreed that a patient is tested in the community by a general practitioner, the general practitioner should undertake testing as indicated in this guide. Ensure arrangements are in place for contacting the patient with the test result – this is the responsibility of the general practitioner.    Cases meeting the suspected case definition for COVID-19 must be tested. Only suspected cases who are in a high-risk category (healthcare workers and residential aged care workers or residential aged care residents) and confirmed cases need to be notified to the department as soon as practicable by calling 1300 651 160, 24 hours a day.      It suggests that whether a person who may be a suspected case of Covid-19 can get tested depends on the determination of a general practice or community health service. Therefore, there are specific requirements that need to be met.    This represents a continuation of the policy of significant changes to pre-covid times as of 23 March 2020 in Victoria.    Note:  The definition of a suspected case is:    A.	If the patient satisfies both clinical and epidemiological criteria, they are classified as a suspected case:    Clinical criteria:  Fever  OR  Acute respiratory infection (for example, shortness of breath or cough) with or without fever    AND    Epidemiological criteria:  International travel in the 14 days before the onset of illness  OR  Close contact in the 14 days before illness onset with a confirmed case of COVID-19    B.	If the patient has severe community-acquired pneumonia (critically ill*) and no other cause is identified, with or without recent international travel, they are classified as a suspected case.  *Critically ill means requiring care in ICU/HDU, or for patients in which ICU care is not appropriate, respiratory or multiorgan failure. Clinical judgement should be exercised considering the likelihood of COVID-19.    C.	If any healthcare worker with direct patient contact, residential aged care worker or aged care resident has a fever (= 37.5) AND an acute respiratory infection (e.g. shortness of breath, cough, sore throat), they are classified as a suspect case. column77: According to the Treasury, the JobKeeper Payment became available introduced from 30 March 2020 until 27 September 2020.    The JobKeeper Payment is a payment made to eligible businesses and not-for-profits affected by the Coronavirus to support them in retaining employees. Businesses must have paid their employees before they are entitled to receive the JobKeeper payment.     Where an employee’s total remuneration is less than $1,500 per fortnight (before tax), or has been stood down, the employer must provide the employee at least $1,500 per fortnight (before tax). Where an employee earns more than $1,500 per fortnight, employers can use the payment to subsidise the employee’s wages.    Self-employed individuals will also be eligible to receive the JobKeeper payment. Self-employed individuals are not informal workers as they operate their own business with an ABN in order to be eligible to the JobKeeper Payment. Therefore, this scheme was available to formal workers.    This represents a 2F level of policy as of 27 April 2020 in Australia. People who meet the following clinical criteria should be tested:  Fever OR chills in the absence of an alternative diagnosis that explains the clinical presentation*  OR  Acute respiratory infection (e.g. cough, sore throat, shortness of breath, runny nose or anosmia).    Note: In addition, testing is recommended for people with new onset of other clinical symptoms consistent with COVID-19** AND who are close contacts of a confirmed case of COVID-19; who have returned from overseas in the past 14 days; or who are healthcare or aged care workers    *Clinical discretion applies including consideration of the potential for co-infection (e.g. concurrent  infection with SARS-CoV-2 and influenza)  **headache, myalgia, stuffy nose, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea    This represents a level 2 policy as of 4 June 2020 in Victoria. column74: International Travel Restrictions    The National Cabinet noted the AHPPC’s advice on high-risk countries for COVID-19 importation risk and its continued support for the 14 day self isolation requirement for all returning travellers. column15: During this period, stage 4 restrictions in metropolitan Melbourne meant that childcare and kindergartens were only open for children who were vulnerable or whose parents were permitted workers. All primary school, secondary school, TAFE and university study was required to be conducted remotely and online, with limited exceptions for vulnerable children and specific TAFE or university courses. column24: Between the 8th and the 14th of August, restaurants and cafes were open for takeaway and delivery only.
